stem.presentation: 85-year-old man with hypertension and paroxysmal AF, not on warfarin after an admission this year for INR 18. Four days earlier he developed dry mouth after starting a BPH medication, which he continued, and called EMS for feeling very dry. In the ED he became tachycardic to 130-140s, irregular, with AF on ECG. IV diltiazem 10 mg x2 had little effect; after 20 mg IV and 30 mg PO diltiazem, HR was 95-115 and SBP 150 to 120. For Cr 1.8 (baseline 1.3) he received 1 L NS, with a second liter hung. On the floor he reported only dry mouth, without palpitations, chest pain, dyspnea, dizziness, nausea, or abdominal pain. HR stayed difficult to control on IV and PO nodal blockers, including IV metoprolol 10 mg; he developed increasing hypoxia, wheezing, and confusion, received IV furosemide 40 mg x2 with minimal result, and was transferred to the CCU.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute on Chronic Systolic (Left Ventricular) Heart Failure (HFrEF, LVEF 30%, NYHA IV) — ICD-10: I50.23 (confidence high).
HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype HFrEF (confidence high); etiology valvular (confidence moderate).

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Unspecified atrial fibrillation, rapid ventricular response; Nonrheumatic aortic (valve) stenosis; Nonrheumatic mitral (valve) regurgitation; Nonrheumatic tricuspid (valve) regurgitation; Other secondary pulmonary hypertension.
COMPLICATIONS: Acute kidney injury, unspecified; Hyperkalemia; Pericardial effusion (noninflammatory); Pleural effusion in other conditions classified elsewhere.

COMORBIDITIES: Essential (primary) hypertension; Benign prostatic hyperplasia; Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified; Chronic kidney disease, unspecified; Gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis.

acute.text: TITRATE UP: furosemide 80 mg IV Q8H.
acute.detail: furosemide: Acute decompensated HFrEF with pulmonary congestion and bilateral pleural effusions Contingency: Hold if SBP <85; reduce if Cr rises >50% from admission or UOP <0.5 mL/kg/hr; consider continuous infusion if bolus doses ineffective. Monitor BMP q12-24h given eGFR 34 and hyperkalemia.

acute.text: START: sodium polystyrene sulfonate 15 g PO once.
acute.detail: sodium polystyrene sulfonate: Acute hyperkalemia management (K 5.6) to enable future GDMT initiation Contingency: Use only if K remains >5.5 after initial diuresis. Recheck K in 4-6 hours. Consider patiromer 8.4 g daily as alternative for sustained K management to facilitate GDMT uptitration.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: metoprolol tartrate 25 mg PO TID; omeprazole 20 mg PO daily; citalopram 20 mg PO daily; lactulose PO BID; ipratropium 0.5 mg NEB Q6H PRN; calcium carbonate PO daily; multivitamin 1 tablet PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
metoprolol tartrate: AF rate control and evidence-based beta-blocker for HFrEF Contingency: Hold if SBP <90 or HR <60; reduce dose if signs of low cardiac output; transition to metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily once euvolemic and stable
omeprazole: GI prophylaxis with concurrent anticoagulation and aspirin Contingency: Beers flag: long-term PPI in age ≥65 — however, active GI prophylaxis indication present (concurrent DOAC + aspirin). Reassess need if aspirin is discontinued. No clopidogrel interaction concern (clopidogrel not prescribed).
citalopram: Depression — chronic home medication Contingency: Max 20 mg daily in age >60 per FDA — at ceiling dose. QTc prolongation risk compounded by digoxin — obtain baseline ECG and monitor QTc q48-72h. Hold or reduce if QTc >500 ms.
lactulose: Chronic home medication for constipation or hepatic encephalopathy prophylaxis
ipratropium: Wheezing — likely cardiac asthma from pulmonary congestion Contingency: Nebulized route (corrected from IV). Discontinue when wheezing resolves with diuresis.
calcium carbonate: Calcium supplementation
multivitamin: Nutritional supplementation

gdmt.text: START: apixaban 2.5 mg PO BID; digoxin 0.0625 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
apixaban: Anticoagulation for AF with CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥5; DOAC preferred over warfarin given prior INR 18 Contingency: Reduced dose (2.5 mg BID) per labeling: age ≥80 AND Cr ≥1.5 (2 of 3 criteria met). No concurrent anticoagulant present — safe to initiate. Hold if active major bleeding. Monitor CBC, Cr weekly inpatient.
digoxin: Adjunctive AF rate control in HFrEF after diltiazem discontinuation Contingency: Beers-compliant at 0.0625 mg (≤0.125 mg/day). Hold if K <3.5 or digoxin level >1.0 ng/mL. eGFR 34 — borderline; if eGFR drops <30, reduce to 0.0625 mg every other day. Check digoxin level in 5-7 days. Monitor K and Cr q24-48h. Monitor QTc (concurrent citalopram).

gdmt.text: START (conditional — see details): dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily; sacubitril-valsartan 24 mg PO BID.
gdmt.detail:
dapagliflozin: GDMT pillar for HFrEF — mortality and HF hospitalization reduction Contingency: Start once hemodynamically stable (SBP ≥95). eGFR 34 is above initiation threshold (≥20). SAFETY FLAG: Triple combination with loop diuretic + ARNi (sacubitril-valsartan when started) increases AKI risk — monitor renal function (BMP) q3d during initiation phase. Hold if recurrent UTI or DKA symptoms. Monitor volume status closely; may need to reduce furosemide dose as patient decongests.
sacubitril-valsartan: GDMT pillar for HFrEF — mortality and HF hospitalization reduction Contingency: DEFER until: K ≤5.0, Cr trending toward baseline (≤1.5), SBP consistently ≥100. Start at 24/26 mg BID. No prior ACEi — no 36h washout needed. Recheck BMP in 1 week after initiation, then q3d if concurrent dapagliflozin and furosemide (triple AKI risk). Hold if SBP <90, K >5.5, or Cr rises >30% from pre-initiation baseline. If not tolerated, substitute losartan 12.5 mg daily.

gdmt.text: HOLD: spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: spironolactone: GDMT pillar for HFrEF — mortality reduction (RALES trial) Contingency: HELD due to K 5.6 and eGFR 34. SAFETY: When sacubitril-valsartan is initiated, combination with spironolactone further increases hyperkalemia risk — do NOT start both simultaneously. Reassess when K <5.0 AND eGFR >30 AND Cr stable AND sacubitril-valsartan tolerated for ≥1 week. Start at 12.5 mg daily with BMP recheck in 3-5 days after initiation. Absolutely contraindicated if K supplement is added.

gdmt.text: TITRATE DOWN: aspirin 81 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: aspirin: Vascular disease; dose reduced from 325 mg given anticoagulation initiation Contingency: Consider discontinuation if no clear coronary indication (no recent ACS/stent) to minimize bleeding risk on DOAC. Aspirin + apixaban increases bleeding risk — reassess at discharge.

monitor.detail: HFrEF (LVEF 30%) + non-DHP CCB is a Class III contraindication. Negative inotropy worsens systolic dysfunction. Rate control achieved with metoprolol tartrate + digoxin. Already marked discontinue by prior audit — removed from curated list entirely.
Mineralocorticoid agonist promotes sodium and water retention — absolutely contraindicated in decompensated HF. Already marked discontinue by prior audit — removed from curated list entirely.
Route was listed as IV but ipratropium is a nebulized medication. Corrected route from IV to NEB.

eGFR 34 (borderline for further dose reduction at <30). Concurrent citalopram increases QTc prolongation risk. Beers criteria require dose ≤0.125 mg/day (compliant at 0.0625 mg). Added: digoxin level at day 5-7, QTc monitoring q48-72h, renal function monitoring, and instruction to reduce to every-other-day dosing if eGFR drops <30.
QTc prolongation risk compounded by concurrent digoxin initiation in 85-year-old. Added baseline ECG and QTc monitoring q48-72h with hold parameter if QTc >500 ms.
SGLT2i + loop diuretic (furosemide) + ARNi (sacubitril-valsartan when started) = triple AKI risk per safety checklist. Added: monitor renal function (BMP) q3d during initiation phase.

Starting ARNi in setting of eGFR 34, K 5.6 (deferred appropriately), with planned concurrent SGLT2i and loop diuretic. Added: BMP q3d once initiated concurrently with dapagliflozin and furosemide. Confirmed no prior ACEi use requiring 36h washout.

Hyperkalemia risk: K 5.6, eGFR 34, with planned sacubitril-valsartan. Appropriately held. Added explicit instruction to not co-initiate with sacubitril-valsartan simultaneously and to never add K+ supplement while on spironolactone.
Iron deficiency is common in HFrEF and IV iron replacement improves symptoms and exercise capacity (Class IIa). Need ferritin and TSAT to assess iron status.
Thyroid dysfunction (both hypo- and hyperthyroidism) can cause or exacerbate heart failure and atrial fibrillation. TSH not documented in current labs.
Serial NT-proBNP trending already initiated (24,117→24,611); repeat at discharge to establish trajectory and guide outpatient management.

Repeat ECG after rate control achieved to assess for underlying conduction disease, QTc monitoring with citalopram + digoxin initiation, and evaluate for amyloid pattern (pseudo-infarct, low voltage) once rate-related changes resolve.

stem.presentation: 83-year-old man with chronic diastolic CHF (EF 50-55%), atrial fibrillation on warfarin, sick sinus syndrome/complete heart block s/p pacemaker, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes presented with 1 week of dyspnea on exertion and orthopnea. He denied chest pain/pressure and peripheral edema but reported heavier legs. He reported adherence to diuretics and a low-sodium diet; his bumetanide had been reduced from 2 mg PO BID to 2 mg PO daily by his nephrologist. His PCP referred him to the ED. ROS was negative for fevers, chills, cough, hemoptysis, black or red stools, and syncope. In the ED, ECG was at baseline, CXR showed a moderate to large right pleural effusion, BNP was 9170 (baseline 6019), and TnT was 0.06. No medications or interventions were given in the ED; he was admitted to Cardiology. First-12 h orders include furosemide 80 mg IV and potassium chloride 40 mEq PO.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute on Chronic Diastolic (Congestive) Heart Failure — HFpEF Exacerbation (ICD-10: I50.32) (confidence high).
HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype HFpEF (confidence high); etiology hypertensive (confidence moderate).

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Malignant pleural effusion, right; Other secondary pulmonary hypertension.
COMPLICATIONS: Pleural effusion in other conditions classified elsewhere; Aspiration pneumonitis due to food and vomit.

COMORBIDITIES: Unspecified atrial fibrillation; Unspecified sick sinus syndrome; Atrioventricular block, complete; Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia; Essential (primary) hypertension; Thyrotoxicosis, unspecified, without thyrotoxic crisis or storm; Anemia, unspecified; Hyperlipidemia, unspecified; Chronic kidney disease, stage 2 (mild).
HISTORY: Presence of cardiac pacemaker.

acute.text: START: furosemide 80 mg IV BID; ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg IV once (repeat in 7 days if needed).
acute.detail:
furosemide: Acute decongestion — volume overload with large pleural effusion, BNP 9170 Contingency: Titrate to UOP >100 mL/hr; switch to IV bumetanide if inadequate response; hold if SBP <90 or Cr rises >50% from baseline. Monitor BMP q6-8h during IV diuresis.
ferric carboxymaltose: Iron deficiency anemia in HF — if TSAT <20% confirmed Contingency: Administer only if TSAT <20% confirmed. Dose based on weight and Hgb per package insert. Monitor for hypersensitivity.

acute.text: TITRATE UP: bumetanide 2 mg PO BID.
acute.detail: bumetanide: Maintenance diuresis — restore prior effective dose that prevented congestion Contingency: Transition from IV diuretics once euvolemic; adjust based on daily weights and volume status; hold if SBP <90 or Cr rises >50%

gdmt.text: START: dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily; spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
dapagliflozin: HFpEF — reduce HF hospitalization Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20; monitor for genital mycotic infections and volume depletion. Monitor BMP (Cr, K) q3d during initiation given concurrent loop diuretic + ACEi (triple AKI risk).
spironolactone: HFpEF — neurohormonal modulation, diuretic synergy Contingency: Hold if K >5.0 or eGFR <30; check BMP in 3 days, then at 7 days, then weekly x4, then monthly. Potassium chloride supplement has been dropped — replete K only if <3.5 with single-dose replacement and recheck.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: trandolapril 2 mg PO daily; metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 10 mg PO daily; methimazole 10 mg PO daily; repaglinide 1 mg PO TID (with meals); insulin SQ per home regimen; calcitriol 0.5 mcg PO daily; folic acid 1 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
trandolapril: HTN, neurohormonal modulation in HF Contingency: Hold if SBP <90, K >5.0 (lowered threshold given concurrent spironolactone), or Cr rises >30% acutely
metoprolol succinate: Rate control for permanent AF, HTN Contingency: Hold if HR <50 (pacemaker backup present, but monitor for symptoms); do not uptitrate during acute decompensation
atorvastatin: Hyperlipidemia Contingency: Consider uptitration if ASCVD documented
methimazole: Hyperthyroidism management — critical for AF and HF control Contingency: Adjust per TSH/free T4; hold if agranulocytosis suspected
repaglinide: Type 2 diabetes Contingency: Monitor for hypoglycemia with SGLT2i initiation; may need dose reduction
insulin: Type 2 diabetes Contingency: Reduce dose by 10-20% with SGLT2i initiation; use inpatient sliding scale
calcitriol: Vitamin D supplementation / mineral bone disease Contingency: Monitor serum calcium
folic acid: Anemia support, home medication

gdmt.text: START (conditional — see details): apixaban 5 mg PO BID.
gdmt.detail: apixaban: Stroke prevention in permanent AF, CHA2DS2-VASc ≥5 Contingency: Reduce to 2.5 mg BID if 2 of 3 criteria met: age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, Cr ≥1.5. Patient meets age criterion (83); confirm weight — if ≤60 kg, reduce dose. Start when INR <2.0 after warfarin discontinuation. Hold for active major bleeding.

gdmt.text: STOP: warfarin PO daily; aspirin 81 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
warfarin: Replaced by apixaban — DOAC preferred over warfarin per guidelines Contingency: Check INR daily; start apixaban when INR <2.0. Do NOT administer warfarin and apixaban concurrently.
aspirin: No indication for concomitant aspirin with full-dose anticoagulation without recent ACS/PCI Contingency: Resume only if new indication arises (ACS, PCI with stent)

gdmt.text: HOLD: ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: ferrous sulfate: Anemia — pending TSAT to confirm iron deficiency Contingency: Check TSAT urgently. If TSAT <20% (iron deficient), switch to IV ferric carboxymaltose and discontinue oral iron. If TSAT ≥20%, continue oral iron and pursue other anemia etiologies.

monitor.detail: ACEi (trandolapril) + spironolactone (newly added) + potassium chloride supplement → high risk of hyperkalemia, especially in an 83-year-old with eGFR 74.7. Per DDI checklist, drop the K+ supplement. Replete only with single-dose replacement if K <3.5 mEq/L with immediate recheck.
SGLT2i + loop diuretic (furosemide IV/bumetanide) + ACEi (trandolapril) = AKI risk triad. Per checklist, monitor renal function (BMP) q3d during SGLT2i initiation. Added to contingency.
Concurrent spironolactone initiation with ACEi in 83-year-old — potassium hold threshold lowered to K >5.0 (from 5.5) in contingency to reflect added hyperkalemia risk after KCl removal.

Patient meets 1 of 3 dose-reduction criteria (age 83 ≥80). Weight is unknown — if ≤60 kg, 2 criteria are met and dose must be reduced to 2.5 mg BID. Contingency updated to flag weight verification as urgent.

Current echo report is incomplete/limited — need formal comprehensive TTE with diastolic assessment, strain imaging (GLS with apical sparing pattern), and wall thickness to confirm HFpEF phenotype, assess for infiltrative features (ATTR amyloidosis), evaluate RV function, and quantify TR/PASP
Patient on methimazole for hyperthyroidism — need TSH and free T4 to assess thyroid control. Uncontrolled hyperthyroidism exacerbates AF and HF.
TSAT (transferrin saturation) needed alongside ferritin 163 to determine iron deficiency (ferritin 100-299 with TSAT <20% = iron deficient in HF). Guides IV iron replacement decision.
Repeat BNP at 48-72h and pre-discharge to assess decongestion response (target >30% reduction from admission BNP of 9170)
Serial ECG monitoring for new ventricular ectopy burden and pacemaker function assessment

stem.presentation: 75-year-old woman with non-small cell lung cancer status post chemotherapy and radiation, COPD, and hypertension, presenting for the third time with dyspnea and hemoptysis. A prior bronchoscopy showed no endobronchial lesions, only generalized submucosal inflammation, and she was discharged on a steroid taper. At the second admission (recurrent dyspnea, milder hemoptysis) she improved with an aggressive COPD regimen. She was discharged on standing inhalers with a 5-day course of cefpodoxime and azithromycin for community-acquired pneumonia; ambulatory O2 sat was 93-97% on room air. After one day at home, she became much more dyspneic after going to the bathroom, following a large meal. She denied chest pain, palpitations, or diaphoresis. Cough had improved, but intermittent rusty sputum persisted. She reported left ankle edema and pain, improved after an 'arthritis pill.' In the ED she received bronchodilators, methylprednisolone, vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, aspirin, and fluids ahead of a planned CTA.

albuterol: COPD exacerbation with diffuse wheezing Contingency: Route corrected from IV to nebulization (inhaled). Use PRN only; hold or reduce frequency if HR >130 or new arrhythmia.

heparin: VTE prophylaxis — active malignancy, immobility, heart failure Contingency: Hold if active significant hemoptysis or platelet count <50K; monitor for HIT if platelets drop >50%. Note: this is prophylactic-dose SQ heparin, NOT therapeutic — no dual anticoagulation concern.

monitor.detail: AGS Beers criteria: benzodiazepine in a 75-year-old patient. Additionally, temazepam poses respiratory depression risk in the setting of acute COPD exacerbation, hypoxia, and pulmonary edema. The prior auditor correctly held this medication; upgrading to DROP for safety. If insomnia management needed, use melatonin 3 mg QHS or trazodone 25 mg QHS.
Route error correction: ipratropium bromide is a nebulized/inhaled medication, not IV. Changed route from 'IV' to 'nebulization' to prevent administration error.
Route error correction: albuterol nebulization solution is administered via nebulizer, not IV. Changed route from 'IV' to 'nebulization' to prevent administration error.

Synergistic nephrotoxicity risk: vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam combination is associated with significantly increased AKI risk, especially concerning in this patient with baseline eGFR 36 and active AKI (Cr 1.5, up from 1.3). Added daily Cr/eGFR monitoring and strong recommendation to switch piperacillin-tazobactam to cefepime 1g IV q12h (renally dosed). Threshold to switch: any Cr rise >0.3 mg/dL.

AGS Beers criteria: long-term PPI use in patient ≥65 without documented GI indication. Currently justified during acute hospitalization (concurrent steroids, hemoptysis, aspirin + heparin). Added explicit reassessment at discharge — discontinue if no ongoing GI indication.

Loop diuretic in patient with eGFR 36 and active AKI, concurrent with ACE-inhibitor-free regimen but with vancomycin/pip-tazo nephrotoxicity risk. Added daily BMP monitoring (K, Mg, Cr) during active diuresis.
IV magnesium repletion in patient with eGFR 36 — risk of hypermagnesemia with impaired renal clearance. Added requirement to check Mg level before each dose to avoid accumulation.

CRITICAL — no echocardiogram has been performed. Need LVEF to commit to HF phenotype (HFrEF vs HFmrEF vs HFpEF), assess wall motion abnormalities, valvular disease, RV function, diastolic function, pericardial effusion size, and pulmonary pressures. This single study will resolve the primary diagnostic uncertainty and dictate GDMT selection.

Iron studies needed to characterize anemia (Hgb 8.4) — ferritin <100 or TSAT <20% would indicate iron deficiency and qualify for IV iron therapy per AHA/ACC Class IIa recommendation in HF with iron deficiency.

Serial troponins q6-8h x3 to confirm downtrending pattern consistent with type 2 MI (demand ischemia) rather than evolving type 1 MI. If troponin rises significantly, would need to reconsider ACS diagnosis.
Thyroid function testing to exclude thyrotoxicosis as contributor to sinus tachycardia and new-onset heart failure. Also relevant as hypothyroidism can cause pericardial effusion.
Recheck BNP in 48-72 hours to assess decongestion response and guide diuretic titration.

stem.presentation: 52-year-old man with multiple sclerosis, a strong family history of premature CAD, and no personal cardiac history. This morning, just after stopping his usual wheelchair-based exercise routine, he had rapid-onset chest heaviness and a general sense of "feeling funny," radiating to the neck, jaw, and left ear and later down the left arm. It eased somewhat on its own but recurred by the time he reached work; he took two sublingual nitroglycerin from his office emergency kit (he is a dentist) with near-complete relief. His PCP referred him to the ED, where the ECG was unremarkable and the initial set of cardiac enzymes was negative. He was given aspirin and metoprolol and started on a heparin drip, and has been pain free since. He reports a viral syndrome with chills about two weeks ago. Cardiac catheterization was performed within the first 12 h (see Cath).

She was seen at home by a provider on the day of presentation, had a HR in the 130s, and was sent to the ED. In the ED, HR was in the 140s and ECG showed a regular narrow-complex tachycardia. apixaban: Stroke prevention in atrial flutter/fibrillation, CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥5 Contingency: Reduce to 2.5 mg BID if ≥2 of: age ≥80 (YES), weight ≤60 kg (confirm), Cr ≥1.5 (NO). If weight ≤60 kg, use 2.5 mg BID. Hold for active major bleeding. TRANSITION: Do NOT administer first dose until heparin drip has been stopped for ≥6 hours. See heparin entry for coordinated timing.
dapagliflozin: HFpEF — reduce HF hospitalizations; diabetes mellitus; CKD Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20. Monitor for genital mycotic infections, UTI, volume depletion. Reduce insulin if hypoglycemia occurs. SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ARB AKI risk: monitor BMP and renal function every 3 days during initiation phase until stable.
spironolactone: HFpEF; potassium-sparing diuretic for hypokalemia management Contingency: Hold if K >5.0 or eGFR <30. Uptitrate to 25 mg daily after 1 week if K <5.0 and Cr stable. Recheck BMP in 3 days, then weekly for first month. Once spironolactone is at steady state and K >4.0, discontinue oral potassium chloride supplementation to avoid hyperkalemia.
potassium chloride: Ongoing potassium repletion for hypokalemia with loop diuretic use Contingency: Reduce to 20 mEq daily once K >3.8. DISCONTINUE once K consistently >4.0 AND spironolactone has been running ≥72 hours. Do NOT continue chronic oral KCl concurrently with spironolactone + valsartan — hyperkalemia risk. Recheck K daily while on supplementation.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: diltiazem 30 mg PO TID; valsartan 160 mg PO daily; insulin SQ per home regimen; docusate sodium 100 mg PO BID; calcium carbonate PO daily; cholecalciferol PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
diltiazem: Rate control for atrial flutter/fibrillation with RVR in HFpEF Contingency: Uptitrate to 60 mg TID or convert to extended-release 120-180 mg daily if HR remains >110 bpm. Hold if SBP <90 or HR <55 bpm. Do not combine with metoprolol.
valsartan: Hypertension, HFpEF, LVH regression, MR reduction Contingency: Hold if SBP <90, K >5.5, or Cr rises >50% from baseline. Monitor BMP in 3 days given concurrent spironolactone and SGLT2i initiation.
insulin: Diabetes mellitus Contingency: Reduce basal/bolus doses by 20% if glucose <140 mg/dL after dapagliflozin initiation. Monitor fingerstick glucose QAC and QHS.
docusate sodium: Constipation prevention
calcium carbonate: Calcium supplementation for bone health Contingency: Discuss risks/benefits given severe mitral annular calcification. Consider dietary calcium as alternative. Separate dosing from other medications by ≥2 hours (reduces absorption of many drugs).
cholecalciferol: Vitamin D supplementation

gdmt.text: HOLD: metoprolol tartrate PO BID.
gdmt.detail: metoprolol tartrate: Previously for rate control/hypertension Contingency: Hold while on diltiazem to avoid excessive bradycardia and AV block. May reinitiate if diltiazem discontinued. Do not use concurrently.

monitor.detail: Dual anticoagulation (heparin + apixaban): Original plan stated 'discontinue 24 hours after first apixaban dose,' which creates dangerous 24-hour overlap of therapeutic heparin and DOAC. Corrected per protocol: stop heparin drip first, wait ≥6 hours, THEN start apixaban. No concurrent administration.

No documented CAD, prior MI, or stents. Concurrent aspirin + apixaban increases bleeding risk without benefit in absence of atherosclerotic indication. Patient age 91 further increases bleeding risk. Already proposed for discontinuation — confirmed and removed from curated list.

Concurrent valsartan (ARB) + spironolactone + potassium supplementation creates hyperkalemia risk. Currently justified by acute hypokalemia (K 3.1), but oral KCl must be time-limited and discontinued once K >4.0 and spironolactone at steady state. Added explicit stop criteria and daily K monitoring.
SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ARB triple combination increases AKI risk. Added renal function monitoring every 3 days during initiation phase per safety checklist.
New spironolactone with concurrent ARB (valsartan) in 91-year-old with CKD 3a (eGFR 53). Added BMP recheck at 3 days and weekly for first month to surveil for hyperkalemia and renal deterioration.
Added explicit transition language: do not administer first apixaban dose until heparin has been stopped for ≥6 hours. Coordinated with heparin entry to prevent dual anticoagulation overlap.
NT-proBNP not measured. Essential for confirming HF diagnosis, assessing severity of congestion, and establishing baseline for monitoring treatment response and discharge readiness.
Rule out thyrotoxicosis as contributor to new-onset atrial flutter/fibrillation. Hyperthyroidism is a reversible cause of AF that must be excluded, especially in elderly patients with new arrhythmia.

TEE recommended to accurately grade MR severity given acoustic shadowing on TTE that may significantly underestimate regurgitation. Critical for determining if MR is severe and amenable to transcatheter intervention.

Iron studies indicated given mild anemia (Hgb 11.3) in setting of HFpEF. Iron deficiency (even without anemia) is common in HF and IV iron repletion improves symptoms and exercise capacity per guidelines.

stem.presentation: 69-year-old man with non-obstructive CAD, CHF with LVEF 45%, HTN, HLD, DMII, peripheral vascular disease, and OSA presented to the ED with progressive dyspnea. Dyspnea began the prior evening and worsened overnight; worse lying flat and with exertion. Denied chest pain, nausea, vomiting, palpitations, dizziness, or lightheadedness. Reports not taking medications as prescribed, non-adherence to dietary restrictions, drinking lots of water at home, and fluid retention. ROS positive for cough; no fevers. In the ED, exam was notable for volume overload; bedside TTE showed LVEF ~25% with global hypokinesis. He received furosemide 20 mg IV once, nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL once, and aspirin 243 mg PO chewed once. Cardiology evaluated him with plan for admission for CHF management and ischemia evaluation. On the floor he reported improvement in dyspnea but not yet back to baseline; denied chest pain, palpitations, fevers, chills, rash, or abdominal pain.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute on Chronic Systolic (Left Ventricular) Heart Failure — Acute Decompensated HFrEF (I50.23) (confidence high).
HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype HFrEF (confidence high); etiology idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (confidence moderate).

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Dilated cardiomyopathy; Patient's noncompliance with other medical treatment and regimen; Dyspnea, unspecified.

COMORBIDITIES: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris; Essential (primary) hypertension; Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia; Raynaud's syndrome / Peripheral vascular disease, unspecified; Peripheral vascular disease, unspecified; Hyperlipidemia, unspecified; Obstructive sleep apnea; Atrioventricular block, first degree; Pneumonia, unspecified organism.
COMPLICATIONS: Hypokalemia; Other specified cardiac arrhythmias (ventricular ectopy).

acute.text: TITRATE UP: furosemide 40 mg IV BID.
acute.detail: furosemide: Acute decompensated HF with volume overload — decongestion Contingency: Target net negative 1-2L/day and UOP >0.5 mL/kg/hr. If inadequate response, escalate to 80mg IV BID or add metolazone 2.5-5mg PO 30 min prior. Transition to PO furosemide 40-80mg daily once euvolemic. Hold if Cr rises >50% or SBP <90.

acute.text: START: magnesium sulfate 2 g IV once.
acute.detail: magnesium sulfate: Magnesium repletion — facilitates potassium repletion and arrhythmia prevention Contingency: Check serum Mg. Maintain Mg >2.0. Transition to oral magnesium oxide 400mg daily if ongoing depletion.

gdmt.text: START (conditional — see details): sacubitril-valsartan 24 mg PO BID; metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily; dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
sacubitril-valsartan: HFrEF LVEF 27% — GDMT pillar 1 (RAAS inhibition with ARNi) Contingency: Hold if SBP <100 or K >5.5 or eGFR <30. Must wait 36 hours after last lisinopril dose. Initiate once decongested and hemodynamically stable.
metoprolol succinate: HFrEF LVEF 27% — GDMT pillar 2 (evidence-based beta-blocker) Contingency: Hold if HR <60 or SBP <90. Uptitrate to 200mg daily as tolerated. Initiate once acute decompensation stabilized — avoid initiation during active volume overload if hypotensive.
dapagliflozin: HFrEF LVEF 27% — GDMT pillar 4 (SGLT2i); dual benefit for comorbid DM2 Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20. Hold during acute illness with dehydration risk. Monitor for genital mycotic infections, UTI. Initiate once acute diuresis phase stabilized and patient tolerating oral intake. SAFETY NOTE: Triple combination with loop diuretic + ARNi increases AKI risk — monitor BMP and renal function q3d during initiation phase. Hold if Cr rises >30% from baseline or signs of hypovolemia.

gdmt.text: STOP: lisinopril 40 mg PO daily; metoprolol tartrate 150 mg PO BID.
gdmt.detail:
lisinopril: Replaced by ARNi (sacubitril-valsartan) Contingency: Must allow 36-hour washout before starting sacubitril-valsartan. If ARNi cannot be initiated (e.g., angioedema, cost), restart lisinopril 40mg daily.
metoprolol tartrate: Not an evidence-based beta-blocker for HFrEF — replaced by metoprolol succinate Contingency: Switch to metoprolol succinate. If succinate unavailable, may temporarily continue tartrate but plan formulary switch.

gdmt.text: START: spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily; potassium chloride 40 mEq PO BID.
gdmt.detail:
spironolactone: HFrEF LVEF 27% NYHA III — GDMT pillar 3 (MRA) Contingency: Hold if K >5.5 or eGFR <30 or Cr rises >30% from baseline. Check BMP at 1 week and 1 month after initiation. Uptitrate to 25mg daily after confirming K <5.0.
potassium chloride: Hypokalemia (K 3.4) — arrhythmia prevention with LVEF 27% and ventricular ectopy Contingency: Target K >4.0 mEq/L. Reduce supplementation as MRA (spironolactone) takes effect. Recheck K with every BMP and at minimum q12h during aggressive repletion. Discontinue supplementation if K >5.0. SAFETY NOTE: Concurrent ARNi + MRA + KCl increases hyperkalemia risk — monitor BMP daily; taper and discontinue KCl once K ≥4.5 and MRA is at steady state.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: amlodipine 10 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily; aspirin 81 mg PO daily; insulin SQ per protocol; heparin 5000 units SQ TID.
gdmt.detail:
amlodipine: Comorbid hypertension — safe in HFrEF (dihydropyridine CCB) Contingency: Reassess need as GDMT is uptitrated and BP improves. Consider dose reduction to 5mg or discontinuation if SBP <110 on optimized GDMT.
atorvastatin: Known CAD, DM2, HLD — high-intensity statin therapy
aspirin: Secondary prevention — known non-obstructive CAD and PVD
insulin: Uncontrolled DM2 (glucose 320) — inpatient glycemic management Contingency: Basal-bolus regimen preferred over sliding scale alone. Target glucose 140-180 mg/dL. Adjust for SGLT2i initiation. Check HbA1c. Coordinate outpatient diabetes regimen optimization at discharge.
heparin: VTE prophylaxis — hospitalized HF patient Contingency: Discontinue at discharge if ambulatory. Monitor platelets for HIT if prolonged use.

gdmt.text: HOLD: isosorbide mononitrate PO daily.
gdmt.detail: isosorbide mononitrate: Unclear indication — no mortality benefit as monotherapy in HFrEF. Reassess for angina indication. Contingency: Hold during acute decompensation. If patient has documented angina, may resume once hemodynamically stable. If no angina indication, discontinue. Do not use concomitantly with ARNi if causing symptomatic hypotension.

monitor.detail: ARNi (sacubitril-valsartan) + MRA (spironolactone) + KCl triple combination poses hyperkalemia risk. K is currently 3.4 requiring acute repletion, so KCl is clinically justified now, but must be tapered aggressively as MRA reaches steady state. Added daily BMP monitoring and explicit taper/stop criteria (discontinue if K ≥5.0, taper when K ≥4.5 with MRA on board).

SGLT2i + loop diuretic (furosemide) + ARNi (sacubitril-valsartan) triple combination increases AKI risk, especially during initiation in a recently decompensated HF patient. Added renal function monitoring q3d during initiation phase and hold criteria for Cr rise >30%.

Comprehensive resting TTE with full Doppler assessment needed — the available study is a stress echo with limited structural/valvular/diastolic evaluation. Need formal diastolic grading (E/e', LA volume index), valvular assessment (functional MR likely with LVEF 27%), LV dimensions, and RVSP estimation. Also serves as baseline for 3-month LVEF reassessment for ICD decision.

Cardiac MRI with LGE and T1 mapping to definitively distinguish ischemic vs non-ischemic cardiomyopathy etiology. Global hypokinesis pattern suggests non-ischemic, but known CAD and new ST-T changes warrant definitive tissue characterization. LGE pattern (subendocardial = ischemic vs mid-wall = non-ischemic) will guide etiology call and long-term management.
Thyroid dysfunction is a reversible cause of cardiomyopathy and should be excluded in any new or worsening HFrEF, per guideline recommendations for initial HF workup.
Iron deficiency (with or without anemia) is common in HFrEF and independently worsens outcomes. Ferritin and TSAT should be checked to evaluate for IV iron candidacy per 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guidelines.

stem.presentation: 49-year-old man with seizure disorder and asthma presenting with heart racing. At 9 AM he had sudden onset of rapid heart rate after drinking a cold 16 oz soda; symptoms persisted all day. A few hours later, getting an item from the refrigerator, he felt lightheaded and as though he would pass out. Denies chest pain or SOB. Has used albuterol nebs more frequently for 3 days (about twice daily) and had recent URI symptoms he believes triggered an asthma flare. Seen in clinic that afternoon in atrial flutter and referred to the ED. ED: atrial flutter at 150; given diltiazem 20 mg IV x 2 and converted to sinus rhythm at around 7, then started on diltiazem 60 mg PO; also received 2 L IVF and aspirin 325. On the floor, feels well without complaints.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: New-onset atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response (I48) (confidence high).
HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype not applicable (confidence high); etiology not applicable (confidence high).

causes.text: COMPLICATIONS: Ventricular tachycardia — rapid ventricular response during atrial flutter; Presyncope/near-syncope; Palpitations (heart racing); Tachycardia, unspecified.
CONTRIBUTORS: Mild persistent asthma with acute exacerbation; Acute upper respiratory infection, unspecified; Adverse effect of antiasthmatics (beta-agonist related arrhythmia trigger).

acute.text: CONTINUE: heparin IV per protocol.
acute.detail: heparin: VTE prophylaxis during hospitalization (subcutaneous prophylactic dosing) or flush line Contingency: Discontinue at discharge. No indication for long-term anticoagulation with CHA2DS2-VASc 0. If therapeutic-dose heparin was used for flutter, confirm step-down to prophylactic dosing now that sinus rhythm is restored.

gdmt.text: START: diltiazem 120 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: diltiazem: Rate control for atrial flutter; maintenance after conversion to sinus rhythm to prevent rapid ventricular response if flutter recurs Contingency: Hold if SBP <90 or HR <50. Uptitrate to 180-240 mg daily if resting HR >110 or symptomatic recurrence. Monitor for interaction with phenytoin (CYP3A4 induction may reduce diltiazem levels). Note: LVEF 60%, structurally normal heart — no HFrEF contraindication. Diltiazem appropriate given asthma (beta-blockers relatively contraindicated).

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: lamotrigine PO per home regimen; phenytoin PO per home regimen; montelukast 10 mg PO daily; fluticasone-salmeterol 250 mcg INH BID; albuterol 2.5 mg INH PRN; ipratropium bromide 0.5 mg INH PRN; levalbuterol 0.63 mg INH PRN; multivitamin 1 tablet PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
lamotrigine: Seizure disorder
phenytoin: Seizure disorder Contingency: Check phenytoin level; note CYP3A4 induction may reduce diltiazem efficacy — monitor rate control adequacy. Also note phenytoin may reduce lamotrigine levels; verify both AED levels are therapeutic.
montelukast: Asthma controller therapy
fluticasone-salmeterol: Asthma controller therapy (ICS/LABA) Contingency: Consider step-up to 500/50 if asthma poorly controlled; ensure proper inhaler technique.
albuterol: Rescue bronchodilator for asthma Contingency: Minimize use; counsel patient that excessive use may trigger atrial arrhythmia recurrence. Prefer levalbuterol if available. Target ≤2 uses/week.
ipratropium bromide: Adjunctive bronchodilator for asthma exacerbation
levalbuterol: Rescue bronchodilator — R-isomer with potentially fewer cardiac side effects Contingency: Consider preferential use over racemic albuterol given atrial flutter history.
multivitamin: Nutritional supplementation

gdmt.text: STOP: aspirin 325 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: aspirin: Given empirically in ED; no ongoing indication with CHA2DS2-VASc 0 and no CAD Contingency: Discontinue at discharge. Aspirin is not recommended for stroke prevention in atrial flutter. No other antiplatelet indication identified.

monitor.detail: Phenytoin is a potent CYP3A4 inducer and will significantly reduce diltiazem plasma levels, potentially rendering rate control inadequate. Conversely, diltiazem (CYP3A4 inhibitor) may modestly increase phenytoin levels. Monitor phenytoin levels and heart rate closely; diltiazem dose may need to be higher than typical to achieve adequate rate control.

monitor.text: SAFETY ADD MONITORING (moderate): salmeterol (in fluticasone-salmeterol) + albuterol + levalbuterol.
monitor.detail: Multiple beta-agonists in a patient with new-onset atrial flutter. Excessive sympathomimetic stimulation may precipitate arrhythmia recurrence. Counsel patient to minimize rescue inhaler use and monitor for palpitations or recurrent tachycardia. Consider consolidating to levalbuterol only (drop racemic albuterol) to reduce cardiac side effects.
Not yet measured. While HF is clinically unlikely given triple-concordant normal findings, a BNP/NT-proBNP would provide definitive biomarker confirmation and serve as a baseline if symptoms recur.

Not documented as drawn. While ACS is clinically unlikely (no chest pain, rate-related ST changes resolved), a troponin should be checked given the rapid rate and ST-T changes on initial ECG to formally exclude demand ischemia.

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic arthropathy (skin and subcutaneous ulcer of foot); Unspecified atrial fibrillation; Ischemic cardiomyopathy.
COMORBIDITIES: Chronic kidney disease, stage 4; Essential (primary) hypertension; Hyperlipidemia, unspecified; Cachexia; Nonrheumatic mitral (valve) insufficiency.
HISTORY: Old myocardial infarction; Presence of aortocoronary bypass graft.
COMPLICATIONS: Primary pulmonary hypertension; Other specified cardiac arrhythmias — ventricular premature beats.

acute.text: TITRATE UP: furosemide 80 mg IV BID.
acute.detail: furosemide: Acute decompensated HF with volume overload — pulmonary edema, bilateral pitting edema with weeping, RA pressure ≥15 mmHg Contingency: Target UOP >100 mL/hr for first 6 hours, then net negative 1-2 L/day. If inadequate response, add metolazone 2.5 mg PO 30 min prior. Tolerate Cr rise up to 0.5 mg/dL if achieving decongestion. Transition to PO furosemide (2.5x IV dose) when euvolemic. Monitor BMP daily given CKD4 baseline and concurrent MRA + ARNi.

acute.text: CONTINUE: vancomycin IV per pharmacy renal dosing protocol.
acute.detail: vancomycin: Diabetic foot ulcer cellulitis — empiric MRSA coverage Contingency: Renal dose adjustment REQUIRED (eGFR 27.6) — expect extended intervals (e.g., q24-48h dosing). Monitor vancomycin troughs or AUC/MIC per protocol. Monitor Cr daily for nephrotoxicity. Vancomycin may potentiate warfarin — monitor INR every 2-3 days. Obtain wound culture to guide de-escalation. Consult ID for duration and transition to oral therapy.

gdmt.text: STOP: lisinopril 2.5 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: lisinopril: HFrEF RAAS inhibition — being replaced by ARNi Contingency: Restart lisinopril 2.5 mg daily if ARNi not tolerated (hypotension, hyperkalemia, AKI). Last dose must be documented with timestamp; sacubitril-valsartan must NOT be given until ≥36 hours after last lisinopril dose.

gdmt.text: START: sacubitril-valsartan 24 mg PO BID; spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
sacubitril-valsartan: HFrEF LVEF 15% — GDMT pillar 1, preferred over ACEi Contingency: Hold if SBP <90, K >5.5, Cr rises >30% from baseline (i.e., Cr >3.1), or symptomatic hypotension. 36-hour washout from lisinopril required before first dose — NEVER administer concurrently with lisinopril (angioedema risk). Check BMP at 3 days and 7 days after initiation. Monitor renal function q3d given eGFR 27.6 and concurrent spironolactone and furosemide.
spironolactone: HFrEF LVEF 15% NYHA III — GDMT pillar 3, MRA for mortality reduction Contingency: Hold if K ≥5.5 or eGFR <20. CAUTION: eGFR 27.6 with concurrent ARNi (valsartan component) — HIGH hyperkalemia risk. Check BMP in 3 days, then every 3 days for first 2 weeks, then weekly for first month. Consider potassium binder (patiromer) if K 5.0-5.5 to allow MRA continuation. Discontinue immediately if K ≥6.0.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID; warfarin 2 mg PO daily; insulin SQ per sliding scale and basal regimen; acetaminophen 500 mg PO every 6 hours PRN.
gdmt.detail:
carvedilol: HFrEF LVEF 15% — GDMT pillar 2, evidence-based beta-blocker; also AF rate control Contingency: Hold if HR <55 or SBP <85. Do not uptitrate during acute decompensation. Uptitrate to 12.5 mg BID once euvolemic and stable.
warfarin: Atrial fibrillation anticoagulation, CHA₂DS₂-VASc 6 Contingency: Monitor INR every 2-3 days during hospitalization — vancomycin interaction may potentiate warfarin effect and raise INR. Target INR 2.0-3.0. If future transition to apixaban is pursued: stop warfarin, check INR daily, start apixaban ONLY when INR <2.0. NEVER administer warfarin and apixaban concurrently. Note: apixaban dose would be 5 mg BID (patient meets only 1 of 3 dose-reduction criteria: age ≥80 NO, Cr ≥1.5 YES, weight ≤60 kg — unknown; verify weight before dosing). Given eGFR 27.6, apixaban is preferred DOAC if transitioning (dabigatran contraindicated at eGFR <30, edoxaban requires CrCl 15-50 for 30 mg dose).
insulin: NIDDM glycemic control — important for wound healing Contingency: Target blood glucose 140-180 mg/dL inpatient. Avoid hypoglycemia. Adjust based on oral intake and renal function (CKD4 with eGFR 27.6 prolongs insulin half-life — reduce basal dose by ~25% from home dose and titrate). Monitor fingerstick glucose QID.
acetaminophen: Pain management — safe analgesic in HF Contingency: Max 2g/day given hepatic congestion from right heart failure. Avoid NSAIDs. Do not exceed 4 doses (2g) in 24 hours.

gdmt.text: START (conditional — see details): dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: dapagliflozin: HFrEF LVEF 15% — GDMT pillar 4, SGLT2i for mortality and HF hospitalization reduction Contingency: DEFER until active diabetic foot ulcer cellulitis is resolving (anticipated 1-2 weeks). SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ARNi with eGFR 27.6 = elevated AKI risk: monitor renal function (BMP) every 3 days during initiation phase. Consider reducing furosemide dose by 25-50% at SGLT2i initiation to mitigate volume depletion. Hold if new genital infection, DKA, worsening foot wound, or eGFR <20. Monitor UOP and volume status closely.

gdmt.text: HOLD: aspirin 81 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: aspirin: Secondary prevention post-MI/CABG Contingency: If CABG >12 months ago and no recent ACS or stent, discontinue aspirin to reduce bleeding risk with concomitant anticoagulation. Discuss with cardiology. Aspirin + warfarin = increased bleeding risk; monotherapy anticoagulation preferred for AF when no recent coronary event.

gdmt.text: TITRATE UP: atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: atorvastatin: ASCVD secondary prevention (CAD s/p MI, CABG) — uptitrate to high-intensity Contingency: Check LFTs at baseline. Reduce to 20 mg if myalgias or transaminases >3x ULN. No renal dose adjustment required.

monitor.detail: Sacubitril-valsartan + ACEi concurrent use causes angioedema. Transition language verified and strengthened: lisinopril must be discontinued with documented timestamp; sacubitril-valsartan must NOT start until ≥36 hours after last lisinopril dose. NEVER concurrent.

Spironolactone + sacubitril-valsartan (ARB component) + CKD4 (eGFR 27.6) = high hyperkalemia risk. Intensified monitoring: BMP every 3 days for first 2 weeks, then weekly. Baseline K 4.3 provides some margin but close surveillance mandatory.

SGLT2i + loop diuretic (furosemide 80 IV BID) + ARNi in CKD4 (eGFR 27.6) = elevated AKI risk. Added renal monitoring q3d during initiation and recommendation to reduce furosemide dose at SGLT2i start.

Warfarin continued for now; future DOAC transition discussed in contingency. Explicit transition protocol added: stop warfarin, start apixaban ONLY when INR <2.0, NEVER concurrent. Dabigatran contraindicated at eGFR <30. Also flagged vancomycin-warfarin interaction requiring INR monitoring q2-3d.

(1) eGFR 27.6 requires renal-adjusted dosing with extended intervals. (2) Vancomycin-warfarin interaction may potentiate anticoagulation — INR monitoring every 2-3 days added. (3) Daily Cr monitoring for nephrotoxicity given CKD4 baseline.
650 mg q6h PRN = potential 2600 mg/day, exceeding stated 2g/day cap for hepatic congestion. Reduced to 500 mg q6h PRN (max 2g/day) to ensure consistency between dose and cap.

Formal 12-lead ECG with precise QRS duration measurement needed to determine CRT-D candidacy. Current ECG reports 'incomplete LBBB' but QRS width not quantified. If QRS ≥150ms with LBBB: Class I CRT indication (in sinus rhythm) / Class IIa in AF. If 120-149ms: Class IIa. This determination directly changes device therapy planning.
Serial NT-proBNP at discharge to assess decongestion trajectory and establish post-diuresis baseline for outpatient monitoring. Current value 30,367 reflects severe congestion.
Thyroid dysfunction is a reversible cause of both HF and AF. TSH should be checked in all new/worsening HF presentations per guidelines. Not documented in current labs.

Iron deficiency is common in HFrEF and independently worsens symptoms and outcomes. Ferritin and TSAT should be checked per 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guidelines (Class IIa, LOE B-R for IV iron repletion if ferritin <100 or ferritin 100-300 with TSAT <20%). Hemoglobin 12.0 does not exclude iron deficiency.
While no acute ACS presentation, baseline troponin helps assess for chronic myocardial injury in advanced HF and rules out subclinical ischemic event contributing to LVEF decline.

stem.presentation: 52-year-old man with hyperlipidemia (LDL 143), glucose intolerance, and history of atypical chest pain. A few days before admission, on a bus, he developed deep, poorly localized, sharp left-sided chest pain worse with deep inspiration, without shortness of breath, nausea, diaphoresis, or radiation. It never resolved and progressively worsened; the day before admission it was exacerbated by bending over, pulling open drawers, or any activity, and was slightly reproducible. Pain was improved on the day of admission; he took no medication at home. Denied recent fevers, chills, cough, trauma, sick contacts, heavy lifting, or exercise. At a scheduled exercise stress test, resting echo showed apical wall motion abnormality with global hypokinesis, EF 30%; no stress test was performed and he was sent to the cath lab: patent vessels, fistula from LAD to pulmonary artery without O2 saturation step-up. Transferred to the floor for monitoring.

gdmt.text: TITRATE UP: lisinopril 5 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: lisinopril: HFrEF LVEF 30% — RAAS inhibition, GDMT pillar 1 Contingency: Hold if SBP <90 or K >5.5 or Cr rises >30% from baseline. Discontinue 36 hours before starting sacubitril/valsartan. Monitor BMP at 1 week and after each dose change given concurrent spironolactone.

gdmt.text: START: carvedilol 3.125 mg PO BID; spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily; dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
carvedilol: HFrEF LVEF 30% — evidence-based beta-blocker, GDMT pillar 2 Contingency: Hold if HR <55 or SBP <85. Uptitrate to 6.25 mg BID in 2 weeks if tolerated, then sequentially to 12.5 mg BID and 25 mg BID.
spironolactone: HFrEF LVEF 30% — MRA, GDMT pillar 3 Contingency: Hold if K >5.5 or eGFR <30. Recheck BMP in 3-5 days (inpatient) and again at 1 week. Uptitrate to 25 mg daily if K <5.0 and Cr stable. Monitor K closely given concurrent lisinopril (ACEi + MRA hyperkalemia risk).
dapagliflozin: HFrEF LVEF 30% — SGLT2 inhibitor, GDMT pillar 4; also beneficial for glucose intolerance Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20. Monitor for genital mycotic infections and volume depletion. Recheck BMP and renal function in 3-5 days during initiation given concurrent ACEi + MRA + SGLT2i (AKI risk with multi-agent RAAS/nephron blockade). Ensure adequate oral intake.
atorvastatin: Hyperlipidemia, LDL 143, primary ASCVD prevention Contingency: Check LFTs at baseline and 3 months. Discontinue if ALT >3x ULN or myopathy develops.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: docusate sodium 100 mg PO BID; heparin 5000 units SQ every 8 hours.
gdmt.detail:
docusate sodium: Stool softener — continue home medication
heparin: VTE prophylaxis during hospitalization; also consider for LV thrombus prevention given severely hypokinetic apex (LVEF 30% with apical akinesis) Contingency: Maintain prophylactic-dose heparin SQ pending cardiac MRI. If LV thrombus identified on MRI: STOP heparin, then initiate therapeutic anticoagulation (warfarin with INR target 2-3 OR apixaban 5 mg BID per 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guidance) — do NOT overlap therapeutic heparin with DOAC. If no LV thrombus: continue prophylactic heparin SQ until discharge, then discontinue.

monitor.detail: NSAID contraindicated in HFrEF (LVEF 30%): causes sodium/water retention, worsens heart failure, and creates 'triple whammy' AKI risk with concurrent ACEi (lisinopril) and MRA (spironolactone). Removed from active prescription list. Patient should be counseled to avoid all NSAIDs; acetaminophen ≤2g/day is the safe alternative.

ACEi (lisinopril) + MRA (spironolactone) combination carries hyperkalemia risk. Baseline K 4.2 is acceptable, but requires close BMP monitoring: recheck in 3-5 days inpatient, then at 1 week, and after any dose titration of either agent.

SGLT2i initiation concurrent with ACEi + MRA represents multi-agent nephron blockade. Although no loop diuretic is currently prescribed and eGFR is normal (102.8), renal function and electrolytes should be monitored every 3-5 days during the initiation overlap period to detect early AKI or electrolyte disturbance.

Heparin route and dose clarified to prophylactic SQ dosing. Added explicit dual-anticoagulation prevention language: if LV thrombus is found and therapeutic anticoagulation (warfarin or DOAC) is initiated, heparin must be STOPPED first — never overlapped with a DOAC. Transition timing specified per guidelines.

Cardiac MRI with T1/T2 mapping and late gadolinium enhancement is the critical discriminating test between Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (no LGE, possible apical edema) and acute myocarditis (subepicardial/mid-wall LGE with edema per Lake Louise Criteria). This will commit the etiology call and determine whether colchicine/immunosuppression is needed.
NT-proBNP/BNP not yet measured. Needed for baseline HF severity assessment, prognostication, and future trajectory monitoring. Class I, LOE A per AHA/ACC/HFSA guidelines.

Serial troponins needed to characterize myocardial injury pattern — rising/falling pattern supports myocarditis; early peak with rapid decline supports Takotsubo. Also needed to quantify degree of myocardial injury.

He developed one hour of mid-sternal chest pain with a band-like, cramping quality. The pain was intermittent and non-radiating, with no precipitating factors. He denied arm or back pain, nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis, and dyspnea. At the presenting facility he was started on a nitroglycerin drip at 28 mcg/min and his pain improved. The drip was increased to 56 mcg/min, with eventual improvement in pain to 0.5/10. He also received aspirin 325 mg, morphine 2 mg IV, and hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV x1. He was then transferred for consideration of cardiac catheterization. On arrival to the CCU he was chest pain free and denied dyspnea.

furosemide: Volume management in HFrEF — minimal bilateral effusions on CXR, compensated Contingency: Increase if weight gain >2 lbs/day or >5 lbs/week, or new dyspnea/edema. Hold if SBP <90 or Cr rises >50% from baseline. Adjust with daily weights. acute.detail:
heparin: Peri-procedural anticoagulation for PCI — no longer needed post-procedure Contingency: Already completed peri-procedural course. No ongoing indication for systemic anticoagulation (no AF detected, bioprosthetic AV >3 months post-op).
morphine sulfate: Acute chest pain — no longer needed, pain resolved Contingency: Chest pain resolved. Morphine may worsen outcomes in ACS per some data and may reduce P2Y12 inhibitor absorption. Avoid routine use.

gdmt.text: START: sacubitril-valsartan 24.26 mg PO BID; metoprolol succinate 25 mg PO daily; dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily; pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
sacubitril-valsartan: HFrEF LVEF 25% — RAAS inhibitor pillar initiation Contingency: Hold if SBP <100, K >5.5, or Cr rises >30% from baseline. Recheck BMP in 3 days and again at 1 week given concurrent spironolactone and eGFR 48.9. Monitor for hyperkalemia closely (K trending 4.2→5.0).
metoprolol succinate: HFrEF LVEF 25% — evidence-based beta-blocker pillar Contingency: Hold if HR <55 or SBP <90. Uptitrate every 2-4 weeks as tolerated to target 200 mg daily.
dapagliflozin: HFrEF LVEF 25% — SGLT2i pillar initiation Contingency: Hold if recurrent UTI or genital mycotic infection. No dose adjustment for eGFR 48.9. Discontinue if eGFR <20 sustained. SAFETY NOTE: Triple combination with furosemide + sacubitril-valsartan increases AKI risk — monitor renal function (BMP) q3d during initiation phase. Hold if Cr rises >30% from baseline. Ensure adequate hydration; consider reducing furosemide if signs of volume depletion.
atorvastatin: Post-ACS high-intensity statin — 3-vessel CAD, NSTEMI, s/p CABG and PCI Contingency: Dose reduced from 80 mg to 40 mg due to concurrent amiodarone (CYP3A4 inhibitor) — FDA max recommendation. Monitor for myalgias and check CK if symptomatic. Reduce further or switch to rosuvastatin if myopathy develops.
pantoprazole: GI prophylaxis with DAPT in elderly patient at high bleeding risk Contingency: Discontinue when DAPT is de-escalated to monotherapy, unless other GI indication. Pantoprazole specifically selected over omeprazole to avoid CYP2C19-mediated clopidogrel interaction.

gdmt.text: STOP: metoprolol tartrate 12.5 mg PO BID.
gdmt.detail: metoprolol tartrate: Replaced by metoprolol succinate — non-evidence-based formulation for HFrEF Contingency: Discontinue once metoprolol succinate is initiated; do not overlap.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: spironolactone 25 mg PO daily; aspirin 81 mg PO daily; clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily; amiodarone 100 mg PO daily; prednisone 40 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
spironolactone: HFrEF LVEF 25% — MRA pillar continuation Contingency: Hold if K ≥5.5 or eGFR <30. Reduce to 12.5 mg if K 5.0-5.4 after ARNi start. Recheck K in 3 days and 1 week. HIGH PRIORITY: K trending toward 5.0 with concurrent sacubitril-valsartan initiation and CKD 3b — monitor BMP q3d for first 2 weeks.
aspirin: Post-PCI DAPT and secondary prevention of ASCVD Contingency: Hold if active GI bleeding. Pantoprazole co-prescribed for GI protection.
clopidogrel: Post-PCI DAPT for NSTEMI/ACS — PTCA to OM2 Contingency: Reassess duration at 6 months — consider de-escalation to aspirin monotherapy if high bleeding events. Do not discontinue prematurely without cardiology consultation. Pantoprazole (not omeprazole) selected for GI protection to avoid CYP2C19 interaction.
amiodarone: Ventricular arrhythmia prophylaxis with ICD Contingency: Monitor TSH q6 months, LFTs q6 months, PFTs annually. Consider discontinuation trial if no VT/VF episodes on ICD interrogation. NOTE: Atorvastatin dose reduced to 40 mg due to amiodarone-statin interaction (CYP3A4 inhibition).
prednisone: Unknown — clarify indication urgently Contingency: If no clear indication, initiate taper (reduce by 5-10 mg/week). Monitor glucose, volume status, and electrolytes. High-dose steroids worsen HF and hyperglycemia. May exacerbate fluid retention — coordinate with furosemide dosing.

monitor.detail: Amiodarone is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Concurrent use with atorvastatin 80 mg increases risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. FDA recommends atorvastatin ≤40 mg with amiodarone. Dose reduced from 80 mg to 40 mg daily.

SGLT2i (dapagliflozin) + loop diuretic (furosemide) + RAAS inhibitor (sacubitril-valsartan) triple combination increases AKI risk. Additionally, sacubitril-valsartan + spironolactone in CKD 3b (eGFR 48.9) with K trending toward 5.0 poses hyperkalemia risk. BMP monitoring q3d added during initiation phase.
SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ARNi ('triple whammy' variant) — AKI risk during initiation. Renal function monitoring q3d added. Consider furosemide dose reduction if volume depletion develops.

Spironolactone + sacubitril-valsartan (RAAS inhibitor) in CKD 3b with K trending 4.2→5.0 — significant hyperkalemia risk. No K+ supplement present (appropriate). Enhanced K monitoring q3d for first 2 weeks; reduce to 12.5 mg if K 5.0-5.4.

NT-proBNP not measured (compute_scores noted absence). Baseline value needed for HFrEF severity assessment, prognostication, and longitudinal monitoring of GDMT response. Critical given LVEF 25% and ACS presentation.
Serial troponins q6-8h x3 needed to trend post-PCI — baseline 0.02, must monitor for periprocedural MI and peak troponin to quantify myocardial injury.
Patient on amiodarone 100mg daily — thyroid function monitoring required (amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis or hypothyroidism). Also relevant as thyroid disease can worsen HF.
Iron deficiency is common in HFrEF and independently associated with worse outcomes. Ferritin and TSAT needed to assess for IV iron therapy candidacy per 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guidelines (Class IIa).

stem.presentation: 82-year-old female with macular degeneration and osteoporosis presenting with ~2 days of progressively worsening burning sensation of the whole left arm, shoulder to fingertips, non-radiating, without chest pain, SOB, palpitations, N/V, or diaphoresis. Two weeks earlier, laryngitis progressed to productive cough; urgent care diagnosed pneumonia and gave inhalers and a 5-day levofloxacin course (completed). PCP follow-up without further intervention; cough persisted. Son noted increased DOE on stairs, and the arm burning began that evening. At the initial presenting facility Trop-T was 0.635 with anterior-septal TWIs on ECG; she received aspirin, was started on heparin, and was transferred. From the ED she went to the cath lab: total RCA occlusion, significant LAD disease treated with a drug-eluting stent, and diagonal disease treated with balloon angioplasty. Loaded with clopidogrel; recovered well in PACU. On the floor she was comfortable, endorsing only non-productive cough.

gdmt.text: START: aspirin 81 mg PO daily; clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily; pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily; sacubitril-valsartan 24 mg PO BID; metoprolol succinate 12.5 mg PO daily; spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily; dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
aspirin: DAPT post-DES for NSTEMI, secondary prevention of ASCVD Contingency: Hold if active bleeding or Hgb <8; resume when stable
clopidogrel: DAPT post-DES for NSTEMI — P2Y12 component Contingency: Hold if active bleeding, Hgb <8, or urgent surgery; reassess duration at 6 months based on DAPT score
pantoprazole: GI prophylaxis with DAPT in elderly patient with mild anemia Contingency: Reassess need when DAPT is de-escalated to aspirin monotherapy; avoid indefinite use per Beers criteria unless ongoing GI indication persists
sacubitril-valsartan: HFrEF GDMT Pillar 1 — LVEF 37%, ischemic cardiomyopathy Contingency: Hold if SBP <100, K >5.5, or Cr rises >30% from baseline; uptitrate to 49/51 mg BID then 97/103 mg BID every 2-4 weeks as tolerated. Monitor BMP at 1 week and 2 weeks after initiation and each uptitration. Do NOT combine with any ACEi; 36h washout required if ACEi is ever considered.
metoprolol succinate: HFrEF GDMT Pillar 2 — evidence-based beta-blocker for mortality reduction Contingency: Hold if HR <55 or SBP <90; uptitrate every 2 weeks toward 200 mg daily as tolerated; monitor QTc given baseline prolonged QT — obtain ECG at baseline and after each uptitration
spironolactone: HFrEF GDMT Pillar 3 — MRA for mortality reduction Contingency: Hold if K >5.0 or eGFR <30; uptitrate to 25 mg daily in 4 weeks if K <5.0 and renal function stable. Monitor BMP at 3 days, 1 week, and 4 weeks after initiation. Concurrent use with sacubitril-valsartan (ARB component) increases hyperkalemia risk — no potassium supplements permitted.
dapagliflozin: HFrEF GDMT Pillar 4 — SGLT2i for mortality and HF hospitalization reduction Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20; monitor for genital mycotic infections and volume depletion. With concurrent sacubitril-valsartan and spironolactone: monitor renal function (BMP) at 3 days, 1 week, and 2 weeks after initiation. Hold if Cr rises >30% from baseline or signs of volume depletion.

gdmt.text: STOP: metoprolol tartrate 6.25 mg PO BID.
gdmt.detail: metoprolol tartrate: Non-evidence-based beta-blocker formulation for HFrEF — replacing with metoprolol succinate Contingency: Discontinue when metoprolol succinate is initiated; do not overlap formulations

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily; heparin 5000 units SQ Q8H; guaifenesin PO BID; ipratropium-albuterol INH Q6H PRN.
gdmt.detail:
atorvastatin: High-intensity statin post-ACS, secondary ASCVD prevention Contingency: Reduce to 40 mg if myalgias or LFTs >3x ULN
heparin: VTE prophylaxis during hospitalization Contingency: Discontinue at discharge. Do NOT continue beyond discharge — patient will be on DAPT which provides partial thromboprophylaxis. If therapeutic anticoagulation is later needed for LV thrombus, stop heparin and initiate warfarin with explicit INR targets; do not overlap with any DOAC.
guaifenesin: Residual cough from recent pneumonia Contingency: Discontinue when cough resolves; reassess if cough persists >2 weeks — note: sacubitril-valsartan has lower cough incidence than ACEi but cough should still be monitored
ipratropium-albuterol: Bronchospasm/cough from recent pneumonia Contingency: Discontinue when respiratory symptoms resolve; monitor HR with albuterol use especially given concurrent beta-blocker (may reduce bronchodilator efficacy and albuterol may counteract rate control — use judiciously)

monitor.detail: Beers criteria flag: PPI use in patient age 82. Current indication (GI prophylaxis on DAPT with mild anemia) is valid and compelling, so retaining. Added explicit reassessment language to discontinue when DAPT is de-escalated, to avoid indefinite use without GI indication.

Spironolactone + sacubitril-valsartan (ARB component) in 82-year-old with estimated eGFR ~50-55: hyperkalemia risk is elevated. Added BMP monitoring at 3 days, 1 week, and 4 weeks. Explicitly prohibited concurrent potassium supplementation. No potassium supplement is currently prescribed, but flagging prophylactically.

SGLT2i initiation concurrent with sacubitril-valsartan and spironolactone in elderly patient with borderline eGFR (~50-55): AKI and volume depletion risk. Added renal function monitoring at 3 days, 1 week, and 2 weeks per SGLT2i + RAAS inhibitor + MRA triple-initiation safety protocol.

Patient has documented prolonged QT interval at baseline. Beta-blockers can further affect QT/QTc. Added ECG monitoring at baseline and after each uptitration to surveil for dangerous QTc prolongation.

Prophylactic heparin SQ concurrent with DAPT (aspirin + clopidogrel) increases bleeding risk. Acceptable inpatient practice post-PCI, but added explicit discharge discontinuation language and guidance for future anticoagulation transitions (e.g., if LV thrombus is detected on surveillance echo, requiring therapeutic anticoagulation with careful transition protocol).

Beta-agonist (albuterol) may partially counteract beta-blocker (metoprolol succinate) and cause tachycardia. Added monitoring note for HR and judicious use. Minor pharmacodynamic interaction but relevant in HFrEF patient on rate-controlling agent.
Baseline BNP/NT-proBNP not yet measured; needed for prognostic stratification in new-onset HFrEF and to establish a baseline for monitoring treatment response to GDMT
TSH not documented; thyroid dysfunction is a reversible contributor to cardiomyopathy and should be excluded in all new-onset HFrEF per guidelines

Iron studies needed to evaluate mild anemia (Hgb 11.5) and assess for iron deficiency — IV iron is indicated in HFrEF with iron deficiency (ferritin <100 or ferritin 100-299 with TSAT <20%) per ESC Class I recommendation

stem.presentation: 64-year-old female with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, hyperglycemia and fibromyalgia (baseline chest/torso pain) developed fairly sudden chest tightness and pressure at 11 pm while watching TV, radiating down the left arm and to the back, without palpitations, dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis or lightheadedness; SL nitroglycerin x1 gave no relief. She noted unusual 'heartburn' before the event and intermittently over the past week. Prior stress MIBI was negative (EF 71%). In the ED, initial ECG showed inferior TWI with cardiac enzymes negative x1; with recurrent chest pain, repeat ECG showed 2 mm inferior STE with STD in I and aVL. Code STEMI was called. She received aspirin, morphine 2 mg IV, metoprolol 5 mg IV x2, heparin bolus, clopidogrel and eptifibatide infusion. At cath, a 90% mid-RCA lesion was stented with a DES after IVUS; an 80% LAD bifurcation lesion was not treated. She now denies chest pain or dyspnea.

acute.detail: eptifibatide: Peri-procedural GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor — discontinue per protocol (typically 18-24h post-PCI) Contingency: Discontinue per standard protocol timing post-PCI

gdmt.text: START: ticagrelor 90 mg PO BID; lisinopril 2.5 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily; metoprolol succinate 25 mg PO daily; pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
ticagrelor: DAPT post-STEMI with DES, more potent P2Y12 inhibition than clopidogrel Contingency: SAFETY NOTE — Ticagrelor + opioid (hydromorphone) DDI: opioids reduce GI absorption and delay onset of ticagrelor antiplatelet effect. Minimize opioid use; if chest pain recurs, do NOT rely on ticagrelor alone — consider IV antiplatelet or parenteral analgesic alternatives. Hold if significant bleeding; reassess at 12 months for continuation vs de-escalation based on ischemic/bleeding risk.
lisinopril: Post-MI secondary prevention, vascular protection, prevent adverse remodeling Contingency: Hold if SBP <90, K >5.5, or creatinine rises >30% from baseline; uptitrate to 10-20 mg daily as BP tolerates. Monitor BMP (K+, Cr) within 1 week of initiation and after each dose titration.
atorvastatin: High-intensity statin for post-ACS secondary prevention, LDL-C reduction Contingency: Check LFTs if symptomatic; reduce to 40 mg if intolerable myalgias (distinguish from fibromyalgia baseline)
metoprolol succinate: Post-MI beta-blocker for secondary prevention, evidence-based formulation Contingency: Hold if HR <55 or SBP <90; uptitrate to 50 mg daily in 2 weeks if tolerated, target up to 200 mg daily
pantoprazole: GI prophylaxis on DAPT; replace ranitidine (withdrawn from market). Pantoprazole selected over omeprazole to avoid CYP2C19 interaction with clopidogrel (if clopidogrel ever resumed). Contingency: Reassess need when DAPT de-escalated to aspirin monotherapy

gdmt.text: STOP: clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily; pravastatin 80 mg PO daily; metoprolol tartrate 25 mg PO; ranitidine PO.
gdmt.detail:
clopidogrel: Replaced by ticagrelor for superior efficacy in STEMI Contingency: Resume clopidogrel 75 mg daily if ticagrelor not tolerated (dyspnea, bleeding). NOTE: if clopidogrel is resumed, use pantoprazole (NOT omeprazole) for GI prophylaxis — already prescribed correctly.
pravastatin: Moderate-intensity statin — insufficient for post-ACS; replaced by atorvastatin 80 mg
metoprolol tartrate: Replaced by metoprolol succinate (evidence-based long-acting formulation)
ranitidine: FDA-withdrawn product; replaced by pantoprazole

gdmt.detail:

monitor.detail: Ticagrelor + opioid (hydromorphone) DDI: opioids delay GI absorption and reduce antiplatelet effect of ticagrelor. This is a known interaction from PLATO sub-analyses. Cannot drop either medication acutely — hydromorphone is a chronic home med for fibromyalgia. Added monitoring language and recommendation to minimize opioid use during acute post-STEMI period.

Concurrent use with ticagrelor reduces antiplatelet efficacy. Concurrent use with lorazepam and gabapentin creates additive CNS/respiratory depression risk. Added contingency language recommending opioid minimization and PCP/pain management referral for de-escalation plan.

Concurrent use with hydromorphone (opioid) and gabapentin poses additive respiratory depression risk (FDA boxed warning for opioid-benzodiazepine combination). Patient is 64 (just under Beers threshold). Added monitoring language. Cannot abruptly discontinue due to withdrawal risk.
Additive CNS depression when combined with hydromorphone and lorazepam. Added sedation monitoring note to contingency.
Patient on levothyroxine 125 mcg for hypothyroidism; confirm euthyroid state as thyroid dysfunction affects cardiovascular outcomes post-MI
Baseline BNP/NT-proBNP not measured; useful for post-MI risk stratification and to definitively exclude subclinical HF given mild diastolic dysfunction and RVSP 40 mmHg

stem.presentation: 71-year-old man with CLL, GERD, HTN, gout, and psoriasis, transferred for urgent catheterization for STEMI. At baseline, walks moderate distances daily. The day before, he had fatigue and episodic right jaw and shoulder pain resolving spontaneously. At about 6 pm, at rest, he developed moderate right jaw, temporal, and shoulder pain ("sore bruise") with mild dizziness, without palpitations, dyspnea, diaphoresis, or nausea. At the outside hospital, SL nitroglycerin and nitroglycerin paste relieved the pain; he was initially treated as NSTEMI with nitroglycerin and heparin infusions while troponin-I rose 0.09 → 1.77 → 21.07. Right radial LHC showed LCx stenosis, treated with a drug-eluting stent; he received a clopidogrel load and an 8-h eptifibatide infusion as bridge to clopidogrel effect. On the floor he has mild right arm pain, less severe and of different quality than the presenting pain, and fatigue; he denies chest pain, dizziness, dyspnea, and orthopnea.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) — Left Circumflex Coronary Artery Territory, Status Post Successful PCI with Drug-Eluting Stent (confidence high).

causes.text: COMPLICATIONS: Chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure with mid-range ejection fraction (HFmrEF); Left anterior fascicular block (atrioventricular block, other and unspecified).
CONTRIBUTORS: Coronary angioplasty status (status post PCI with DES); Long-term (current) use of anticoagulants/antithrombotics (long-term use of antiplatelet agents); Weakness/fatigue.

COMORBIDITIES: Essential (primary) hypertension; Chronic lymphocytic leukemia of B-cell type; Gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis; Gout, unspecified; Psoriasis; Nonrheumatic aortic (valve) stenosis — mild/trivial aortic valve disease; Hyperlipidemia, unspecified; Chronic pulmonary embolism — ruled out (pulmonary hypertension, borderline).
HISTORY: Dissection of aorta, unspecified site — ruled out (mildly dilated ascending aorta).

acute.text: START: nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL PRN.
acute.detail: nitroglycerin: Rescue therapy for recurrent anginal symptoms post-STEMI Contingency: Do not use if SBP <90 or if PDE5 inhibitor taken within 24-48 hours

gdmt.text: START: aspirin 81 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily; lisinopril 5 mg PO daily; metoprolol succinate 25 mg PO daily; dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily; spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily; pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
aspirin: Secondary prevention post-STEMI, DAPT component Contingency: Hold if active bleeding or platelet count <50k
atorvastatin: High-intensity statin post-ACS for secondary prevention and HF prevention Contingency: Reduce to 40 mg if myalgias or ALT >3x ULN; discontinue if rhabdomyolysis
lisinopril: Post-MI LV dysfunction (LVEF 45%), HFmrEF, HTN Contingency: Hold if SBP <90, K >5.5, or Cr rises >30% from baseline. Uptitrate to 10-20 mg at 2-week intervals as tolerated. Consider transition to sacubitril-valsartan if LVEF remains ≤45% at 3-month reassessment. NOTE: Patient is on concurrent spironolactone — do NOT add potassium supplements. Monitor K and Cr at 3 days, 1 week, and 1 month after co-initiation.
metoprolol succinate: Post-MI beta-blocker, HFmrEF, HR control Contingency: Hold if HR <55 or SBP <90. Uptitrate by 25-50 mg every 2 weeks toward target 200 mg daily as tolerated.
dapagliflozin: HFmrEF — reduce HF hospitalization and CV death Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20. Monitor for volume depletion, UTI, genital mycotic infections. No dose adjustment needed. NOTE: Co-prescribed with ACEi (lisinopril) — monitor renal function (BMP) at 3 days and 1 week after initiation to assess for AKI risk.
spironolactone: HFmrEF (LVEF at lower end of spectrum), post-MI remodeling prevention Contingency: Hold if K >5.5 or eGFR <30. Check K and Cr at 3 days, 1 week, and 1 month. Uptitrate to 25 mg daily if K remains <5.0. IMPORTANT: Co-prescribed with lisinopril — hyperkalemia risk elevated. Absolutely NO exogenous potassium supplementation unless K <3.5 with close monitoring.
pantoprazole: GERD; GI prophylaxis on DAPT Contingency: Reassess need at 12 months when DAPT may be de-escalated. Preferred over omeprazole to minimize CYP2C19 interaction with clopidogrel.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: clopidogrel: DAPT post-DES for STEMI — P2Y12 inhibitor component Contingency: Hold if active bleeding, platelet count <50k, or need for urgent surgery. Consider switch to ticagrelor 90 mg BID if no contraindication and no excess bleeding risk.

monitor.detail: ACEi + MRA combination increases hyperkalemia risk, especially in a 71-year-old. Baseline K is 4.0 (acceptable). Added explicit monitoring cadence (BMP at 3 days, 1 week, 1 month) and strict prohibition on potassium supplementation to both prescription contingencies. Current K 4.0 and Cr 0.83 support safe co-initiation with close surveillance.

SGLT2i + ACEi co-initiation can increase AKI risk via hemodynamic effects on GFR. No loop diuretic is present (mitigating the full 'triple whammy'), but given age 71 and multiple new agents, added renal function monitoring at 3 days and 1 week post-initiation.

Beers criteria flag: long-term PPI use in patient ≥65. However, this patient has a documented GERD indication AND is on DAPT (GI prophylaxis indication), AND pantoprazole is correctly chosen over omeprazole to avoid CYP2C19 interaction with clopidogrel. Retained with note to reassess at 12 months when DAPT de-escalation may allow PPI discontinuation or step-down to H2RA.
NT-proBNP not measured during this admission. Baseline value needed for HFmrEF prognostication and to establish a trajectory reference point for future monitoring.
Serial troponins to confirm peak and downtrend post-PCI. Last value was 21.07 — need to document declining trajectory to confirm successful reperfusion.
Thyroid function not assessed. Hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism can contribute to cardiomyopathy and are modifiable. Standard workup for new-onset LV dysfunction.
Iron deficiency is common in HF and independently worsens outcomes. Ferritin and TSAT should be checked to assess for iron deficiency requiring IV iron repletion per ESC guidelines.

stem.presentation: 83-year-old man with CAD, chronic systolic CHF (EF 40%), HTN, HLD, CKD, peripheral vascular disease, and one prior episode of atrial fibrillation following epistaxis, presenting with dyspnea and chest pain. Flu-like symptoms 2 weeks earlier; a cold with sinus congestion, cough, and cold sore around dyspnea onset. Chest pain 2-3 days earlier resolved with 2 sublingual nitroglycerin; dyspnea progressed, worse with exertion and lying flat, with pinkish phlegm, increased edema, and ~9 lb weight gain (now 209 lb). ED: furosemide 20 mg IV. Floor: heparin drip for NSTEMI started then discontinued; furosemide drip (down 1.5 L at 5 pm); SBP trended from 160s/90s to 100s/40s. At 11 pm, atrial fibrillation with RVR; BP trended down after metoprolol, 500 cc bolus given, amiodarone considered, transferred to CCU. Alert, oriented x3, denying chest pain or dyspnea; HR ~120s despite 5 mg IV metoprolol, with MAP falling to ~55.
stem.home_meds: From first-12 h orders: lisinopril 10 mg PO/NG, metoprolol tartrate 100 mg PO/NG, isosorbide mononitrate ER 60 mg PO, aspirin 325 mg PO/NG, clopidogrel 75 mg PO/NG, atorvastatin 80 mg PO/NG, ranitidine 150 mg PO/NG, allopurinol 100 mg PO/NG, ascorbic acid 500 mg PO/NG
