dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute on Chronic Systolic (Left Ventricular) Heart Failure — Acute Decompensated HFrEF (LVEF 30%, NYHA Class IV) (confidence high).
HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype HFrEF (confidence high); etiology ischemic (confidence high).

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI); Unspecified atrial fibrillation; Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris; Nonrheumatic mitral (valve) regurgitation; Tricuspid insufficiency.
HISTORY: Old myocardial infarction.
COMPLICATIONS: Primary pulmonary hypertension; Hyperkalemia; Hypo-osmolality and hyponatremia.
COMORBIDITIES: Chronic kidney disease, stage 4; Essential (primary) hypertension; Hyperlipidemia, unspecified; Other specified peripheral vascular diseases; Anemia, unspecified.

acute.text: CONTINUE: furosemide 20 mg/hr IV continuous infusion.
acute.detail: furosemide: Acute decongestion for ADHF with pulmonary edema and pleural effusions Contingency: Titrate to UOP >100 mL/hr; hold if SBP <85 or Cr rises >50% from baseline; add metolazone 2.5 mg PO daily if inadequate diuresis

acute.text: STOP: heparin IV continuous infusion.
acute.detail: heparin: Bridge anticoagulation for NSTEMI and new AF Contingency: STOP heparin drip 6 hours BEFORE first apixaban dose. Do NOT co-administer heparin and apixaban (dual anticoagulation → major bleeding risk). If unable to take PO, continue heparin drip with aPTT monitoring until PO is feasible, then stop 6h before apixaban.

acute.text: START: amiodarone 150 mg IV bolus then infusion (1 mg/min x 6h, then 0.5 mg/min x 18h); calcium gluconate 1000 mg IV once; insulin regular 10 units IV once.
acute.detail:
amiodarone: Acute rate/rhythm control for AF with RVR refractory to IV metoprolol in hemodynamically unstable HFrEF Contingency: If sinus rhythm restored, transition to PO amiodarone 200 mg TID x 1 week, then 200 mg BID x 1 week, then 200 mg daily. Monitor QTc (hold if >500 ms), TSH, LFTs at baseline and q3 months. SAFETY NOTE: Amiodarone + atorvastatin — monitor for rhabdomyolysis (myalgias, dark urine, CK). Amiodarone + apixaban — amiodarone is a P-gp inhibitor; apixaban levels may increase modestly; dose already reduced to 2.5 mg BID, no further adjustment needed but monitor for bleeding.
calcium gluconate: Emergent cardiac membrane stabilization for hyperkalemia (K 5.9-6.1) with AF and PVCs Contingency: Administer over 5-10 min. Repeat if ECG changes persist. Does not lower K — must pair with insulin/dextrose and potassium binder.
insulin regular: Intracellular potassium shift for hyperkalemia (K 5.9-6.1) Contingency: Give with 25g dextrose (D50 50 mL). Monitor glucose q1h x 4h. Repeat if K remains >5.5 after 1 hour.

acute.text: START (conditional — see details): patiromer 8.4 g PO daily.
acute.detail: patiromer: Sustained potassium lowering to enable MRA and ACEi/ARNi initiation in HFrEF with CKD Contingency: Start once acute hyperkalemia managed. Titrate to maintain K 4.0-5.0. Separate from other oral medications by ≥3 hours. May increase to 16.8 g daily if K remains >5.0.

acute.text: HOLD: nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL PRN.
acute.detail: nitroglycerin: Breakthrough chest pain Contingency: Hold while SBP <100. May use cautiously if SBP >110 and symptomatic angina.

gdmt.text: HOLD: lisinopril 10 mg PO daily; metoprolol tartrate 100 mg PO BID; isosorbide mononitrate 60 mg PO daily; allopurinol 100 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
lisinopril: Home ACEi for HFrEF Contingency: Hold for hyperkalemia (K 5.9-6.1), hypotension (MAP 55), and acute decompensation. Restart at 2.5-5 mg daily when SBP >100, K <5.0, Cr stable. Plan transition to sacubitril-valsartan after 36h washout. SAFETY NOTE: Lisinopril and sacubitril-valsartan must NEVER be co-administered — mandatory 36h washout before ARNi initiation (angioedema risk).
metoprolol tartrate: Home beta-blocker (non-evidence-based formulation) Contingency: Hold during acute decompensation with hemodynamic instability (MAP 55, AF with RVR). Convert to metoprolol succinate once stable.
isosorbide mononitrate: Home anti-anginal Contingency: Hold for hypotension (MAP 55). Reassess need once on optimized GDMT. Restart at 30 mg daily only if persistent angina despite beta-blocker and revascularization.
allopurinol: Gout prophylaxis Contingency: Hold during acute illness. Restart at 100 mg daily (CKD-adjusted dose) once clinically stable.

gdmt.text: START (conditional — see details): sacubitril-valsartan 24 mg PO BID; metoprolol succinate 12.5 mg PO daily; dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
sacubitril-valsartan: ARNi for HFrEF — superior to ACEi for mortality reduction Contingency: Start only after: (1) K <5.0, (2) SBP >100 consistently, (3) Cr stable, (4) 36h washout from last lisinopril dose — NEVER co-administer with lisinopril (angioedema risk). Hold if SBP <90 or K >5.5. If not tolerated, resume lisinopril 2.5-5 mg daily after 36h washout from sacubitril-valsartan.
metoprolol succinate: Evidence-based beta-blocker for HFrEF mortality reduction Contingency: Start only when euvolemic, SBP >100, HR >60, no active decompensation. Uptitrate every 2 weeks as tolerated to target 200 mg daily. Hold if SBP <90 or HR <55.
dapagliflozin: SGLT2i for HFrEF — reduces HF hospitalization and CV death Contingency: Start once SBP >95 and hemodynamically stable. No dose adjustment needed for eGFR 30.7. Hold if eGFR <20. Monitor for volume depletion, UTI, genital mycotic infections. SAFETY NOTE: Patient will be on SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ACEi/ARNi — monitor renal function (BMP) q3d during initiation phase for AKI risk. Hold if Cr rises >30% acutely.

gdmt.text: START: apixaban 2.5 mg PO BID; famotidine 20 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
apixaban: Anticoagulation for AF (CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥4) and LV thrombus prophylaxis (apical akinesis) Contingency: Dose-reduced to 2.5 mg BID (age 83 + Cr 2.1 meets ≥2 of 3 criteria: age ≥80, Cr ≥1.5). TRANSITION: Stop heparin drip 6 hours BEFORE first apixaban dose. Do NOT overlap. Monitor for bleeding. If GI bleed, reassess dose-reduction criteria at that time.
famotidine: GI prophylaxis — replacement for ranitidine; GI protection during triple antithrombotic therapy Contingency: If higher GI bleeding risk with triple therapy and PPI needed, use pantoprazole 40 mg daily — NOT omeprazole (CYP2C19 interaction with clopidogrel).

gdmt.text: TITRATE DOWN: aspirin 81 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: aspirin: NSTEMI — DAPT component; reduced dose due to concurrent anticoagulation Contingency: Reduce from 325 mg to 81 mg immediately given triple therapy (aspirin + clopidogrel + apixaban). SAFETY: Triple therapy limited to ≤1 week given high bleeding risk (age 83, CKD, anticoagulation). Discontinue aspirin after 1 week; continue clopidogrel + apixaban (dual pathway). Reassess if high ischemic event occurs.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
clopidogrel: P2Y12 inhibitor for NSTEMI with prior stents and 3-vessel CAD Contingency: Continue for up to 12 months post-NSTEMI. After aspirin discontinuation, dual pathway therapy (clopidogrel + apixaban). Reassess duration based on bleeding vs ischemic risk at 6-12 months. SAFETY NOTE: If PPI needed for GI protection, use pantoprazole — NOT omeprazole (CYP2C19 interaction reduces clopidogrel efficacy).
atorvastatin: High-intensity statin for ACS and severe 3-vessel CAD Contingency: Check LDL in 4-6 weeks. If LDL >70 mg/dL, add ezetimibe 10 mg daily. Monitor LFTs. SAFETY NOTE: Amiodarone is being initiated — amiodarone can increase statin levels. Atorvastatin max recommended dose with amiodarone is 40 mg/day per some guidelines. However, given ACS with severe 3-vessel CAD, 80 mg is maintained with close monitoring for myalgias, CK elevation, and rhabdomyolysis symptoms. Check CK if symptoms develop.

monitor.text: SAFETY ADD TRANSITION (major): heparin + apixaban (dual anticoagulation).
monitor.detail: Original prescription proposed 24h overlap of heparin drip + apixaban, which constitutes concurrent dual anticoagulation and carries major bleeding risk. CORRECTED: Heparin must be stopped 6 hours BEFORE the first apixaban dose. No overlap period. Transition language updated on both heparin and apixaban prescriptions.

monitor.text: SAFETY MODIFY DOSE (major): aspirin + clopidogrel + apixaban (triple antithrombotic therapy).
monitor.detail: Triple therapy (aspirin + P2Y12 + DOAC) carries high bleeding risk, especially in 83-year-old with CKD. Duration shortened from '1-4 weeks' to '1 week' maximum per guidelines for high-bleeding-risk patients. Aspirin already appropriately reduced to 81 mg.

Sacubitril-valsartan + ACEi concurrent use causes angioedema. Both prescriptions already include 36h washout language, but explicit reinforcement added: NEVER co-administer. Lisinopril is held; sacubitril-valsartan contingency requires 36h washout confirmed.

monitor.text: SAFETY ADD MONITORING (moderate): dapagliflozin (SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ACEi/ARNi).
monitor.detail: SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ACEi/ARNi combination ('triple whammy' variant) increases AKI risk, particularly in CKD stage 3b (eGFR 30.7) with baseline Cr 2.1. Added monitoring: BMP q3d during initiation phase; hold if Cr rises >30%.

Amiodarone inhibits CYP3A4 and increases statin exposure, raising rhabdomyolysis risk. Some guidelines recommend capping atorvastatin at 40 mg with amiodarone. Given compelling ACS indication for 80 mg, maintained with enhanced monitoring: check CK if myalgias develop, counsel patient on symptoms of rhabdomyolysis.
Ranitidine withdrawn from market (NDMA contamination). Already appropriately replaced with famotidine in proposed list. Confirming removal.

monitor.text: SAFETY ADD MONITORING (moderate): apixaban (renal dose check).
monitor.detail: Apixaban dose-reduction criteria met: age 83 (≥80) + Cr 2.1 (≥1.5) = 2 of 3 criteria. Dose correctly reduced to 2.5 mg BID. Confirmed appropriate. Monitor renal function; if Cr normalizes and only 1 criterion remains, reassess for full-dose 5 mg BID.

monitor.text: SAFETY ADD MONITORING (moderate): clopidogrel + omeprazole (preventive flag).
monitor.detail: Clopidogrel is on the list; famotidine contingency mentions possible PPI escalation. Explicit warning added: if PPI needed, use pantoprazole — NOT omeprazole (CYP2C19 interaction reduces clopidogrel antiplatelet effect).
Not yet measured. NT-proBNP needed for prognostication, baseline for discharge comparison, and monitoring treatment response in ADHF. Also helps risk-stratify for advanced HF therapies.
Baseline thyroid function required before amiodarone initiation (amiodarone causes both hypo- and hyperthyroidism). Also, thyroid disease can contribute to AF and HF.

Iron deficiency is common in HF and independently worsens outcomes. Hct 32.8% with CKD — need ferritin and transferrin saturation to assess for IV iron candidacy (Class IIa recommendation in HFrEF with iron deficiency).
Formal 12-lead ECG with measured QRS duration needed once sinus rhythm restored — CRT candidacy assessment requires QRS ≥150ms with LBBB morphology. Current ECGs do not report QRS duration.

Cardiac MRI with LGE would definitively characterize ischemic scar burden, assess myocardial viability for revascularization planning (CABG candidacy), and exclude LV thrombus (echo could not fully exclude). Also evaluates for any superimposed non-ischemic pathology.

stem.presentation: 60-year-old woman with CAD (prior coronary angiogram without intervention; later angiogram with 60% mid LAD and 80% distal LAD stenosis, managed medically), asthma/COPD (did not tolerate metoprolol), and chronic diabetic neuropathy with an insulin pump. Since earlier this year, chest pressure in the left chest and ears with throat tightness, about 5 min at a time, occasionally with shortness of breath and diaphoresis, relieved by sublingual nitroglycerin; exercise tolerance fell from walking 3.5 miles to 10 min. With persistent daily episodes, she presented for elective catheterization after contrast-allergy premedication (prednisone, diphenhydramine, ranitidine). Stents were placed in the mid and distal LAD, with a small distal dissection. With balloon expansion she had throat tightness and nausea, then hypotension requiring IABP (replaced after distal migration) and dopamine infusion. On CCU arrival, chest pain had improved to slight discomfort without dyspnea. Prior BRBPR attributed to hemorrhoids, none recently.
stem.home_meds: From first-12 h orders: bupropion SR 300 mg PO, citalopram 40 mg PO/NG, omeprazole 40 mg PO, ipratropium-albuterol neb, lorazepam 0.5 mg PO/NG, insulin 20 units SC, insulin 0 units SC. Note also mentions clopidogrel (previously initiated), sublingual nitroglycerin for chest pain, insulin pump; metoprolol not tolerated.

causes.text: COMPLICATIONS: Intraoperative cardiac arrest during cardiac surgery; ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction involving left anterior descending coronary artery; Postprocedural hypotension; Coronary artery dissection; Acute pulmonary edema.

COMORBIDITIES: Right bundle-branch block, unspecified; Atrioventricular block, first degree; Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia; Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, unspecified; Asthma, unspecified; Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified; Gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis; Left anterior fascicular block; Generalized anxiety disorder.

acute.text: START: nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL PRN chest pain.
acute.detail: nitroglycerin: Symptomatic relief of residual angina Contingency: Do not use if SBP <90. May repeat every 5 min x3 doses; if no relief, activate EMS.

acute.text: TITRATE DOWN: dopamine IV continuous infusion.
acute.detail: dopamine: Hemodynamic support for procedural hypotension Contingency: Wean by 2 mcg/kg/min every 30-60 min. Hold wean if MAP <65 or SBP <90. Target complete discontinuation.

acute.text: CONTINUE: heparin IV continuous infusion.
acute.detail: heparin: Anticoagulation for IABP Contingency: Discontinue upon IABP removal. Monitor aPTT per protocol (target 60-80 sec). Hold if platelet count <50,000 or active bleeding. Monitor CBC daily for HIT screening (platelet count trend). Note: concurrent use with DAPT increases bleeding risk — monitor for signs of bleeding q4h, maintain hemoglobin checks daily.

gdmt.text: START: aspirin 81 mg PO daily; clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily; pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
aspirin: DAPT post-DES, secondary prevention of ASCVD Contingency: Hold if active GI bleeding or platelet count <50,000
clopidogrel: DAPT post-DES placement in mid-LAD, prevention of stent thrombosis Contingency: Do not discontinue without cardiology approval. Hold if major bleeding or urgent surgery required. Use pantoprazole (not omeprazole) for GI prophylaxis to avoid CYP2C19 interaction.
atorvastatin: High-intensity statin for secondary prevention of ASCVD with DM Contingency: Reduce dose if ALT >3x ULN or intolerable myalgias with elevated CK
pantoprazole: GI prophylaxis on DAPT — switched from omeprazole to avoid CYP2C19 inhibition reducing clopidogrel efficacy Contingency: Reassess need upon DAPT completion. Consider step-down or discontinuation if no ongoing GI indication.

gdmt.text: START (conditional — see details): lisinopril 2.5 mg PO daily; bisoprolol 1.25 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
lisinopril: Secondary prevention post-PCI/periprocedural MI, DM with CAD, renoprotection Contingency: Hold if SBP <90, K >5.5, or Cr rises >30% from baseline. Do not start until dopamine weaned and hemodynamically stable ≥6 hours. Monitor BMP at 72h after initiation.
bisoprolol: Secondary prevention post-periprocedural MI, cardioselective beta-blocker chosen due to asthma/COPD Contingency: Hold if HR <55, SBP <90, or new-onset bronchospasm/wheezing. Do not start until dopamine weaned and hemodynamically stable ≥6 hours. Discontinue and switch to ivabradine if bronchospasm occurs.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: insulin SQ continuous via pump; bupropion PO daily; citalopram PO daily; ipratropium-albuterol INH PRN or per home regimen; acetaminophen 650 mg PO every 6 hours PRN.
gdmt.detail:
insulin: Type 2 diabetes mellitus management Contingency: Target glucose 140-180 mg/dL inpatient. Glucose gel and glucagon available for hypoglycemia.
bupropion: Depression
citalopram: Depression Contingency: Monitor QTc; ensure dose ≤20 mg given age approaching 60 per FDA guidance. Discontinue if QTc >500 ms.
ipratropium-albuterol: COPD/asthma maintenance and rescue Contingency: Use before bisoprolol dosing if symptomatic. Increase frequency if bronchospasm develops on beta-blocker.
acetaminophen: Pain management — preferred analgesic (avoid NSAIDs) Contingency: Max 3g/day. Avoid if ALT >3x ULN.

monitor.detail: Major DDI: Omeprazole is a potent CYP2C19 inhibitor that significantly reduces clopidogrel activation to its active metabolite, diminishing antiplatelet efficacy. This is critical post-DES placement where stent thrombosis risk is high. Replaced with pantoprazole 40 mg daily, which has minimal CYP2C19 inhibition.
Substituted for omeprazole to avoid clopidogrel interaction. Reassess GI indication upon DAPT completion; long-term PPI use without clear indication should be avoided.

Concurrent heparin infusion (for IABP) with DAPT (aspirin + clopidogrel) increases bleeding risk. Added explicit monitoring: aPTT per protocol, daily CBC with platelet trend for HIT screening, bleeding assessment q4h, and clear discontinuation trigger upon IABP removal.

Initiating ACEi in a post-procedural patient who required vasopressor support. Added BMP monitoring at 72h post-initiation to assess potassium and renal function. Contingency already appropriately requires hemodynamic stability before starting.

Serial troponins every 6-8 hours x3 to trend periprocedural myocardial injury (type 4a MI) and monitor for evolving ischemia from distal coronary dissection. Current troponin 0.05 — need to determine peak and trajectory.

Serial ECGs every 12 hours x 48 hours to monitor T-wave evolution in anterior/lateral leads and assess for new ischemic changes from distal dissection. Baseline shows RBBB + LAFB with nonspecific T-wave changes.
Not yet measured. Would help establish baseline and clarify whether CXR pulmonary congestion represents subclinical elevated filling pressures vs. purely iatrogenic volume overload.

stem.presentation: 81-year-old man with moderate aortic stenosis (1.0 cm2 on echo), CAD, and renal insufficiency s/p renal stenting, with continued angina despite nitrates, admitted directly (observation) for pre-cath hydration. He reports progressively worsening exertional chest pain and SOB over several months, first noted before a prior cath and now occurring with minimal exertion such as walking across the room; he avoids stairs. Pain is substernal, radiating to the right side of the chest and occasionally the back, without radiation to neck, jaw, or arms and without diaphoresis or nausea. An episode of pain at rest prompted him to seek further intervention. He denies PND, orthopnea, significant ankle edema, palpitations, syncope, or presyncope. He had prolonged bleeding after a prior cystoscopy, with subsequent procedures well tolerated. He denies prior stroke, TIA, DVT, PE, or black or red stools. IV sodium bicarbonate 150 mEq was ordered.

COMORBIDITIES: Chronic kidney disease, stage 4; Essential (primary) hypertension; Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia; Anemia, unspecified; Bradycardia, unspecified; Nonrheumatic aortic (valve) insufficiency; Gout, unspecified; Hyperlipidemia, unspecified; Benign prostatic hyperplasia.

acute.text: START: sodium polystyrene sulfonate 15 g PO once, may repeat x1; sodium chloride 0.9% 1 mL/kg/hr IV continuous.
acute.detail:
sodium polystyrene sulfonate: Hyperkalemia correction (K 5.5) prior to catheterization Contingency: Recheck K in 4-6 hours. If K remains ≥5.5, repeat dose or consider IV calcium gluconate and sodium zirconium cyclosilicate if available. Do not proceed to cath until K <5.0.
sodium chloride 0.9%: Contrast-induced nephropathy prevention in CKD stage IV Contingency: Reduce rate to 0.5 mL/kg/hr if signs of pulmonary congestion (crackles, SpO2 drop, dyspnea). Monitor I&O, daily weights, lung exam Q4H. Monitor BMP daily during IV hydration given eGFR 27.8.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: aspirin 81 mg PO daily; clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily; simvastatin 40 mg PO daily; metoprolol succinate 25 mg PO daily; isosorbide mononitrate PO daily; allopurinol PO daily; tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO daily; insulin SQ per home regimen with inpatient sliding scale; trazodone PO QHS; polyethylene glycol 17 g PO daily; docusate sodium 100 mg PO BID; senna 8.6 mg PO daily PRN; acetaminophen 650 mg PO Q6H PRN; multivitamin 1 tablet PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
aspirin: Secondary prevention of CAD Contingency: Hold if active bleeding or platelet count <50,000
clopidogrel: DAPT for known CAD with prior stenting Contingency: Hold 5-7 days pre-SAVR if surgical route chosen; coordinate with Heart Team for TAVR. NOTE: omeprazole switched to pantoprazole to avoid CYP2C19 interaction reducing clopidogrel efficacy.
simvastatin: High-intensity statin for CAD secondary prevention Contingency: Consider outpatient switch to atorvastatin 40-80 mg for true high-intensity therapy. If macrolide antibiotics are started, hold statin.
metoprolol succinate: CAD, anti-anginal, rate control Contingency: Hold if HR <50 or SBP <100. Do not uptitrate given baseline bradycardia (HR 54). Monitor closely post-TAVR for high-degree AV block.
isosorbide mononitrate: Exertional angina Contingency: Hold if SBP <100 or pre-syncope/syncope. Use cautiously in severe AS (fixed cardiac output). Reassess need post-TAVR.
allopurinol: Gout prophylaxis Contingency: MANDATORY: Verify dose ≤100-200 mg/day for eGFR ~28 (dose reduction required in CKD stage IV). Hold if rash or hypersensitivity reaction. Recheck uric acid level and renal function in 2 weeks.
tamsulosin: BPH Contingency: Hold if orthostatic hypotension. Additive hypotension risk with isosorbide mononitrate and trazodone — monitor orthostatics.
insulin: Diabetes mellitus Contingency: Reduce dose by 25% given CKD stage IV (reduced insulin clearance, eGFR 27.8). Monitor fingerstick glucose Q6H. Dextrose 50% and glucagon at bedside.
trazodone: Insomnia Contingency: Hold if orthostatic hypotension or QTc prolongation. Beers criteria flag (sedating medication in age 81) — use lowest effective dose. Monitor for falls risk given concurrent tamsulosin, isosorbide, metoprolol.
polyethylene glycol: Constipation — also aids potassium excretion
docusate sodium: Stool softener
senna: Constipation PRN
acetaminophen: Pain management — safe in CKD Contingency: Max 2g/day
multivitamin: Nutritional supplementation

gdmt.text: HOLD: valsartan PO daily.
gdmt.detail: valsartan: BP control and CAD secondary prevention — currently held for hyperkalemia Contingency: Restart at reduced dose once K <5.0 mEq/L and eGFR stable. Recheck BMP 48h after restart. Do NOT add ACEi or potassium supplements while on valsartan given CKD IV and hyperkalemia history.

gdmt.text: SUBSTITUTE: pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: pantoprazole: Gastroprotection on DAPT with anemia — switched from omeprazole to avoid clopidogrel DDI Contingency: Reassess PPI need periodically; long-term PPI use flagged under Beers criteria (age 81) but justified here by concurrent DAPT and anemia (Hgb 10.4) suggesting possible GI blood loss.

monitor.detail: Clopidogrel + omeprazole DDI: omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing clopidogrel activation and antiplatelet efficacy. Replaced with pantoprazole 40 mg daily, which has minimal CYP2C19 interaction. PPI indication retained (gastroprotection on DAPT with anemia Hgb 10.4).

Beers criteria: long-term PPI use in patient age 81. Justified by concurrent DAPT and anemia suggesting GI blood loss risk. Reassess need periodically; consider H. pylori testing and GI evaluation for anemia.

Heparin appears on home medication list (likely flush/prophylactic). Confirm this is sodium chloride 0.9% flush and/or SQ prophylactic dosing only, NOT therapeutic anticoagulation. If therapeutic heparin is active, clarify indication and ensure no concurrent anticoagulant overlap. Patient is on DAPT — adding therapeutic heparin increases bleeding risk significantly.

Hyperkalemia (K 5.5) with eGFR 27.8 on ARB. Appropriately held in proposed list. Ensure BMP recheck before any restart. Do NOT add ACEi, spironolactone, or potassium supplements. If restarted, recheck BMP at 48h and 1 week.

Renal dose adjustment required: eGFR 27.8 (CKD stage IV). Allopurinol dose should not exceed 100-200 mg/day per renal dosing guidelines. Verify current home dose and reduce if >200 mg/day. Risk of allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome increases with renal impairment and inappropriate dosing.
Renal dose adjustment: eGFR 27.8 reduces insulin clearance. Reduce total daily dose by ~25% from home regimen. Monitor fingerstick glucose Q6H to avoid hypoglycemia. Already reflected in contingency.

Beers criteria flag: sedating medication in 81-year-old. Increased fall risk compounded by concurrent hypotensive agents (tamsulosin, isosorbide, metoprolol). Use lowest effective dose. Monitor orthostatics and fall risk daily.

monitor.text: SAFETY ADD MONITORING (moderate): sodium chloride 0.9% IV.
monitor.detail: IV hydration in patient with eGFR 27.8, moderate AS, and pulmonary hypertension (RVSP 52). Risk of volume overload. Monitor I&O, daily weights, lung auscultation Q4H, SpO2 continuously. Reduce rate or stop if pulmonary congestion develops. Check BMP daily.
Coronary angiography planned this admission to assess CAD burden and guide combined revascularization + valve intervention strategy. Pre-cath hydration underway.

No BNP/NT-proBNP available. Would help distinguish whether hemodynamic abnormalities (elevated RVSP, elongated LA) represent subclinical HFpEF vs isolated valvular hemodynamics. Would also serve as baseline before valve intervention.

Anemia workup (Hgb 10.4) — iron studies including ferritin, TIBC, and transferrin saturation to differentiate iron deficiency (possible GI loss on DAPT) from CKD-related anemia. Guides IV iron vs EPO therapy.
Rest angina episode warrants troponin to formally exclude NSTEMI, though stable ECG and normal wall motion make ACS less likely.
Repeat ECG after hyperkalemia correction to confirm resolution of any subclinical conduction effects and establish new baseline before catheterization.

stem.presentation: 59-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, PVD s/p SFA, and a history of intermittent claudication. Starting about 10 days before admission he had exertional chest pressure. It first came on with mild activity (household chores, lifting), then with less and less activity until bending down brought it on. The pain spread to the upper back and upper arms. He denied dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis, positional or food relation, lightheadedness, leg pain on walking, orthopnea, PND, ankle edema, palpitations, and syncope. At the referring hospital he was chest-pain free, ECG was unremarkable, CXR was negative, and troponin was 0.02. He was transferred for cardiac catheterization, which showed three-vessel disease with a diagonal lesion not optimal for PCI. Cardiac surgery was consulted, with pre-operative workup this admission and return for CABG after clopidogrel washout. IV heparin was ordered. On arrival to the floor he was hemodynamically stable and chest-pain free.

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris (three-vessel coronary artery disease); Presence of aortocoronary bypass graft (anticipated CABG).

COMORBIDITIES: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia; Essential (primary) hypertension; Hyperlipidemia, unspecified; Atherosclerosis of other type of bypass graft(s) of the extremities / Peripheral vascular disease status post SFA intervention; Occlusion and stenosis of bilateral carotid arteries; Atherosclerosis of aorta; Other spondylosis with myelopathy, cervical region / Degenerative changes of thoracic spine; Long term (current) use of aspirin; Long term (current) use of oral hypoglycemic drugs / insulin; Insomnia, unspecified; Hypokalemia.

acute.text: CONTINUE: nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL PRN chest pain.
acute.detail: nitroglycerin: Breakthrough angina relief while awaiting CABG Contingency: Hold if SBP <90. If chest pain unrelieved after 3 doses q5min, activate ACS protocol.

gdmt.text: TITRATE DOWN: aspirin 81 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: aspirin: Secondary prevention in NSTE-ACS with three-vessel CAD, perioperative and post-CABG Contingency: Hold if active GI bleeding; continue through CABG

gdmt.text: STOP: clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: clopidogrel: DAPT for NSTE-ACS; must washout ≥5 days before CABG Contingency: Discontinue at least 5 days before scheduled CABG date. Resume post-CABG per cardiac surgery team. If CABG delayed >5 days and recurrent ischemia, may restart with surgical team agreement.

gdmt.text: TITRATE UP: metoprolol tartrate 25 mg PO BID.
gdmt.detail: metoprolol tartrate: Anti-ischemic therapy for NSTE-ACS, rate/BP control, perioperative AF prophylaxis for CABG Contingency: Hold if HR <55 or SBP <100. Titrate to resting HR 55-65 bpm. Do NOT discontinue abruptly pre-CABG — continue perioperatively to reduce AF risk.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: lisinopril 10 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily; hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg PO daily; insulin SQ per home regimen; heparin 5000 units SQ TID; potassium chloride PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
lisinopril: Secondary prevention in CAD with DM and HTN; reduces CV events Contingency: Hold if SBP <90, K >5.5, or creatinine rises >30% from baseline. Hold morning of CABG per anesthesia. Monitor BMP q3d while co-administered with potassium chloride.
atorvastatin: High-intensity statin for ACS and very high-risk ASCVD; plaque stabilization pre-CABG Contingency: Monitor LFTs if symptoms of myopathy or hepatotoxicity. Target LDL <70 mg/dL.
hydrochlorothiazide: Hypertension management Contingency: Hold if SBP <100, hyponatremia <130, or hypokalemia <3.5. Hold perioperatively if hemodynamically unstable. Monitor BMP q3d while inpatient.
insulin: DM Type II glycemic control; perioperative glucose target 140-180 mg/dL Contingency: Transition to basal-bolus + sliding scale perioperatively. Monitor fingerstick glucose QAC and QHS.
heparin: VTE prophylaxis during inpatient stay awaiting CABG; transition from therapeutic peri-catheterization heparin Contingency: Discontinue therapeutic IV heparin; transition to prophylactic SQ dosing. Confirm therapeutic IV heparin has been stopped before initiating prophylactic SQ dosing. Resume therapeutic dosing if recurrent ischemic symptoms. Monitor platelets q2-3d for HIT surveillance given prior therapeutic heparin exposure.
potassium chloride: Electrolyte supplementation with concurrent HCTZ use Contingency: Adjust based on serum K. Hold if K >5.0. Increase if K <3.5. Monitor BMP q3d while co-administered with lisinopril. Risk of hyperkalemia with concurrent ACEi — maintain K target 3.5-5.0 mEq/L.

gdmt.text: START (conditional — see details): empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: empagliflozin: Cardiovascular risk reduction in T2DM with established ASCVD (EMPA-REG OUTCOME); renal protection Contingency: Do NOT start until post-CABG recovery with adequate oral intake. Hold ≥3 days pre-surgery. Do not start if eGFR <20. Monitor for genital mycotic infections and euglycemic DKA. Monitor BMP within 1 week of initiation given concurrent lisinopril and HCTZ.

monitor.detail: Concurrent lisinopril (ACEi) + potassium chloride carries hyperkalemia risk. HCTZ partially offsets K+ retention, but close monitoring is required. Added BMP q3d monitoring and explicit K+ hold threshold to potassium chloride and lisinopril contingencies.

Patient was on therapeutic IV heparin peri-catheterization and is transitioning to prophylactic SQ heparin. Added explicit confirmation language to ensure therapeutic heparin is discontinued before prophylactic dosing begins, and added HIT surveillance (platelet monitoring q2-3d) given prior therapeutic heparin exposure.

Appropriately held perioperatively in proposed list, but given upcoming CABG with post-operative respiratory depression risk, opioid use (oxycodone-acetaminophen on home meds), and fall risk in the surgical setting, zolpidem should be dropped from the inpatient curated list entirely. Can be reassessed as outpatient post-recovery.
Baseline BNP not drawn. While heart failure is clinically excluded, a baseline value is useful for pre-CABG risk stratification and future comparison if symptoms develop post-operatively.
Initial troponin 0.02 at outside hospital. Serial troponin at receiving facility would confirm negative biomarker trajectory and solidify unstable angina vs NSTEMI distinction.
Pre-operative thyroid function screening — hypothyroidism can affect perioperative hemodynamics and recovery; hyperthyroidism can exacerbate angina and arrhythmia risk.

stem.presentation: 63-year-old man with a history of PAD and CAD, admitted for ambulatory observation, reporting chest pain and bilateral leg pain. Leg pain is worsening, left worse than right, present at rest and worse with walking; he must use a motorized chair when grocery shopping. He has described left-sided chest discomfort since his last coronary stenting. A catheterization report documents rotational atherectomy, PTCA and non-overlapping DES to the proximal/mid and distal RCA. Cardiac catheterization showed LMCA 60-70% distal, LCX 80% origin, RCA occluded mid and 90% proximal, patent renals and iliacs, 90% right popliteal, and 70% SFA and 80% popliteal on the left; plan is CABG with SFA/popliteal PTA later. Echocardiogram and carotid ultrasound were to be obtained. He denies prior stroke, TIA, DVT, PE, bleeding at surgery, hemoptysis, black or red stools, or recent fevers, chills or rigors.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Atherosclerotic heart disease — multivessel coronary artery disease requiring CABG (confidence high).
HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype HFmrEF (confidence high); etiology ischemic (confidence high).

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Chronic stable angina pectoris; Atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities with rest pain, bilateral legs; Chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure; Old myocardial infarction; Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure.

COMORBIDITIES: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia; Hypothyroidism, unspecified; Atrioventricular block, first degree; Hyperlipidemia, unspecified; Obesity, unspecified; Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified; Nonrheumatic aortic (valve) stenosis; Atherosclerosis of other arteries — aortic atherosclerosis.
HISTORY: Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft.

acute.text: START: furosemide 20 mg PO daily.
acute.detail: furosemide: Volume optimization for elevated LV filling pressures (PCWP >18) pre-CABG Contingency: Titrate to euvolemia; hold if hypotensive or hypovolemic; reassess need after SGLT2i initiation. SAFETY FLAG: Part of SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ACEi triple combination — monitor renal function q3d and daily weights; reduce or hold furosemide if signs of overdiuresis or Cr rise >0.3 mg/dL.

gdmt.text: TITRATE DOWN: aspirin 81 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: aspirin: Secondary prevention CAD/PAD, DAPT with clopidogrel post-DES Contingency: Hold if active bleeding; hold morning of CABG per surgical protocol

gdmt.text: START: clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily; dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily; spironolactone 25 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
clopidogrel: DAPT after recent RCA DES placement; secondary prevention for PAD Contingency: Hold 5 days before CABG surgery; resume post-CABG per surgical team. If PPI needed for GI prophylaxis, use pantoprazole (NOT omeprazole — clopidogrel-omeprazole DDI reduces antiplatelet effect).
dapagliflozin: HFmrEF GDMT pillar; T2DM cardiovascular benefit Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20; hold 3 days before CABG (euglycemic DKA risk); resume when tolerating PO post-op. SAFETY FLAG: Triple combination with furosemide + lisinopril increases AKI risk — monitor BMP and renal function q3d during initiation phase; hold dapagliflozin and furosemide if Cr rises >0.3 mg/dL from baseline.
spironolactone: MRA for HFmrEF with elevated filling pressures Contingency: Hold if K >5.0 or eGFR <30; recheck BMP in 3 days and again at 1 week after initiation; hold perioperatively if K trending up. Do NOT add potassium supplements while on lisinopril + spironolactone (hyperkalemia risk).

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily; lisinopril 40 mg PO daily; metoprolol succinate 150 mg PO daily; insulin regular human U-500 225 units SQ BID; levothyroxine 125 mcg PO daily; venlafaxine 150 mg PO daily; trazodone 25 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
atorvastatin: High-intensity statin for ASCVD (CAD, PAD, DM) Contingency: Monitor LFTs if symptoms of myopathy; continue perioperatively
lisinopril: HFmrEF, post-MI, hypertension, diabetic nephroprotection Contingency: Hold if SBP <90, K >5.5, or AKI; hold morning of CABG per anesthesia protocol. Monitor K+ closely given concurrent spironolactone — recheck BMP in 3 days after spironolactone initiation and weekly thereafter.
metoprolol succinate: Evidence-based beta-blocker for HFmrEF, post-MI, rate control Contingency: Hold if HR <55 or SBP <90; monitor PR interval given 1st degree AV block; do not uptitrate if PR >280ms or symptomatic bradycardia
insulin regular human U-500: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with severe insulin resistance Contingency: AM dose 225 units, PM dose 200 units; adjust with endocrine input; may need dose reduction after SGLT2i initiation (additive glucose-lowering effect — monitor BG QID); perioperative insulin drip protocol for CABG
levothyroxine: Hypothyroidism Contingency: Take on empty stomach; check TSH pre-CABG
venlafaxine: Depression Contingency: Do not abruptly discontinue; coordinate perioperative management
trazodone: Depression/insomnia Contingency: Monitor for orthostatic hypotension

monitor.text: SAFETY ADD MONITORING (moderate): dapagliflozin + furosemide + lisinopril.
monitor.detail: SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ACEi triple combination increases AKI risk per safety checklist. All three agents are clinically indicated (HFmrEF GDMT + volume management), so none are dropped, but renal function monitoring q3d during initiation is mandatory. Added explicit monitoring language and hold parameters to dapagliflozin and furosemide contingencies.

ACEi + MRA combination carries hyperkalemia risk. No potassium supplement is present (appropriate). Added explicit BMP monitoring at 3 days and 1 week, K+ threshold of 5.0 for hold, and explicit prohibition on adding potassium supplements.
Preemptive safety note added to contingency: if PPI is needed for GI prophylaxis, use pantoprazole only — omeprazole reduces clopidogrel antiplatelet effect via CYP2C19 inhibition.

monitor.text: SAFETY ADD MONITORING (moderate): insulin regular human U-500.
monitor.detail: SGLT2i initiation will have additive glucose-lowering effect on top of high-dose U-500 insulin (425 units/day total). Added monitoring for hypoglycemia (BG QID) and note that insulin dose reduction may be needed after dapagliflozin is started.
NT-proBNP not measured; needed to establish baseline for HFmrEF monitoring, confirm elevated filling pressures, and guide GDMT optimization. Compute_scores noted NT-proBNP not available.
Pre-CABG thyroid function assessment; patient on levothyroxine — need to confirm euthyroid state before cardiac surgery. Hypothyroidism can worsen HF and increase perioperative risk.
Baseline troponin not documented; recent catheterization with RCA intervention — need to assess for periprocedural myocardial injury and establish baseline pre-CABG.
Post-catheterization ECG to confirm no new ischemic changes after RCA intervention and establish baseline PR interval for beta-blocker monitoring.

stem.presentation: 65-year-old man with CAD s/p DES to LAD who presented for a routine stress echo ordered by his PCP. He retired 3 days ago. On the treadmill he developed left shoulder pain similar to his previous anginal pain, with ST changes on EKG. The pain resolved after he stopped and he returned to baseline. Per the HPI, echo showed 4+ aortic regurgitation (1+ on his last echo). He exercises 3 times per week and notices faint chest pain only with maximal exercise. He denies shortness of breath, PND, orthopnea, lower extremity edema, palpitations, syncope, presyncope, fevers, chills, night sweats and weight loss. He was sent straight to the ED, where an EKG reportedly showed no ischemic changes and CTA chest was negative for aortic dissection. He was admitted to cardiology. He is currently asymptomatic but considerably distressed by the new diagnosis.

He was recently admitted for intractable cough, diagnosed with HCAP and COPD exacerbation, treated with vancomycin/ceftazidime and prednisone, and discharged to rehab. CT during that stay incidentally showed a bronchopulmonary process concerning for pneumonia vs neoplasm, with follow-up recommended. He now presents from rehab with 4 days of left-sided chest pain at the nipple area. The pain is dull and nonradiating, worse with exertion and relieved by rest, with mild dyspnea. He denies nausea/vomiting, diaphoresis, palpitations, lightheadedness and syncope. He was afebrile at rehab with BPs in the 110s. In the ED, bedside ultrasound showed a large pericardial effusion. He was tachypneic and placed on 4 L NC, and received an arterial line, 3 L NS and 2 U FFP. On the floor, chest discomfort was mild and improved. He is wheelchair-bound due to his legs and has 45-degree orthopnea at baseline.

gdmt.detail:
sacubitril-valsartan: HFrEF LVEF 30%, NYHA III — GDMT Pillar 1 Contingency: Hold if SBP <100 or K >5.5 or Cr rises >30% from baseline. Do not initiate until ≥48h post-pericardiocentesis and hemodynamically stable. Monitor BMP (Cr, K) q3d during initiation — triple AKI risk with concurrent SGLT2i + loop diuretic. Uptitrate every 2-4 weeks as tolerated to 97/103 mg BID.
carvedilol: HFrEF LVEF 30%, NYHA III — GDMT Pillar 2; also AF rate control Contingency: Hold if HR <55 or SBP <90. Monitor for COPD exacerbation/bronchospasm — if occurs, switch to bisoprolol 1.25 mg daily. Ensure pacemaker provides adequate rate support before uptitration.
dapagliflozin: HFrEF LVEF 30% — GDMT Pillar 4; renoprotection in CKD Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20. Monitor BMP q3d during initiation given concurrent loop diuretic + sacubitril-valsartan (triple AKI risk). Monitor for volume depletion and UTI given suprapubic catheter.
colchicine: Effusive-constrictive pericarditis — anti-inflammatory therapy to reduce recurrence and resolve pericardial inflammation Contingency: Hold if GI intolerance (diarrhea), WBC <3000, or eGFR <30. Avoid concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor renal function q1-2 weeks given eGFR 51.8 (CKD stage 3b) — colchicine clearance is reduced in renal impairment; dose is acceptable at current eGFR but requires vigilance.
vitamin K (phytonadione): Reversal of supratherapeutic INR (4.1) in setting of hemorrhagic pericardial effusion Contingency: Administer if INR remains >3.0 after FFP. Recheck INR 6-12 hours post-administration. May repeat once if INR still >2.5.
atorvastatin: HFrEF of likely ischemic etiology (extensive infarct pattern on ECG, possible regional WMA); secondary cardiovascular prevention in 77-year-old male with multiple risk factors Contingency: Monitor LFTs at baseline and 3 months. Hold if ALT >3x ULN or myopathy symptoms. Consider moderate-intensity (atorvastatin 20 mg) if poorly tolerated.

gdmt.detail:
spironolactone: HFrEF LVEF 30%, NYHA III — GDMT Pillar 3 Contingency: DEFER initiation until K confirmed <5.0 on 2 consecutive checks and SGLT2i established (typically 3-5 days). Discontinue if K >5.5 or Cr >2.5. Check K and Cr at 3 days and 1 week after initiation. Heightened hyperkalemia risk: concurrent sacubitril-valsartan (ARB component) + eGFR 51.8 + baseline K 4.6. No potassium supplements to be administered concurrently.
apixaban: Stroke prevention in AF, CHA2DS2-VASc ≥4. DOAC preferred over warfarin per guidelines. Contingency: TRANSITION PROTOCOL: Do NOT start until INR <2.0 (warfarin discontinued), pericardial drain removed, repeat echo confirms no reaccumulation, ≥48-72h hemostatic stability. NEVER overlap with warfarin. Current dose-reduction assessment: age 77 (<80), Cr 1.4 (<1.5), weight unknown — standard 5mg BID appropriate. Reassess for 2.5mg BID if Cr rises ≥1.5 or weight confirmed ≤60kg (need 2 of 3 criteria). Monitor CBC for bleeding given Hgb 8.3.

Administer vitamin K 2.5 mg PO x1 if INR remains >3 after FFP. NEVER administer warfarin and apixaban concurrently.

stem.presentation: 78-year-old man with CAD (RCA stent years ago), aortic stenosis (0.7 cm2), and COPD. In the days before admission he noted slightly worsening dyspnea, needing to go slowly up 1 flight of stairs; he normally participates in rehab with cardiovascular exercise and does housework without difficulty. On the day of admission to an outside hospital he awoke with sudden severe dyspnea and cough productive of significant yellow phlegm; no fevers, chills, chest discomfort, or palpitations. Troponin-I was elevated and CXR reportedly raised concern for pneumonia. He received ceftriaxone, azithromycin, IV steroids, and nebs; dyspnea improved dramatically after the first neb. Stress test showed mild lateral wall ischemia. Cardiac cath showed an 80% RCA lesion appearing to be in-stent restenosis, not intervened; right heart cath showed PA pressures in the mid-40s and mean aortic valve gradient 31 mm Hg. He was transferred for consideration of further interventions.

acute.text: START: furosemide 20 mg IV daily.
acute.detail: furosemide: Mild pulmonary congestion on CXR, Group 2 PH with PA pressures mid-40s Contingency: Hold if SBP <100 or Cr rises >0.5 from baseline. Avoid aggressive diuresis in severe AS (preload-dependent). Monitor BMP daily (K+, Cr, Na). Transition to PO when euvolemic.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: losartan 100 mg PO daily; metoprolol succinate 12.5 mg PO daily; isosorbide mononitrate 120 mg PO daily; clonidine 0.3 mg PO daily; aspirin 81 mg PO daily; clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily; ipratropium-albuterol INH Q6H then PRN; prednisone 40 mg PO daily; azithromycin 250 mg PO daily; heparin 5000 units SQ Q8H; docusate sodium 100 mg PO BID; multivitamin 1 tablet PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
losartan: Hypertension, neurohormonal blockade in setting of HF/severe AS Contingency: Hold if SBP <100, K >5.5, or Cr rises >30% from baseline. Monitor BMP (K+, Cr) daily while inpatient given baseline K 4.9, eGFR 47, and concurrent furosemide.
metoprolol succinate: Heart rate control, CAD, potential HFrEF (pending LVEF); cardioselective beta-blocker safe in COPD Contingency: Hold if HR <50 or SBP <90. Do not uptitrate until LVEF known and post-valve intervention
isosorbide mononitrate: Hypertension, angina prophylaxis in CAD with severe AS Contingency: Hold if SBP <110; consider downtitration peri-TAVR. Use caution with vasodilators in severe AS — preload-dependent physiology.
clonidine: Hypertension (non-preferred agent; continue to avoid rebound) Contingency: Beers criteria flag (age 78): central alpha-agonist associated with CNS adverse effects, orthostasis, and bradycardia in elderly. Do NOT abruptly discontinue — rebound hypertension risk. Begin gradual taper (reduce by 0.1 mg/week) when BP controlled on other agents. Hold if SBP <100 or HR <50. Monitor for orthostatic hypotension and sedation.
aspirin: Secondary prevention of CAD, peri-TAVR antiplatelet therapy Contingency: Hold if active GI bleeding
clopidogrel: CAD with in-stent restenosis, DAPT for potential TAVR Contingency: Hold if active bleeding or platelet count <50K. Note: pantoprazole (not omeprazole) selected to avoid CYP2C19 interaction.
ipratropium-albuterol: COPD exacerbation with productive cough and dramatic bronchodilator response Contingency: Transition to PRN as symptoms improve. Monitor HR
prednisone: COPD exacerbation Contingency: Monitor blood glucose Q6H while on steroids. Discontinue after 5-day course complete. Monitor K+ (steroids may partially offset hyperkalemia risk from losartan/CKD).
azithromycin: Possible lower respiratory tract infection with productive yellow sputum Contingency: Monitor QTc (obtain baseline and repeat EKG day 3). Discontinue after course complete. Reassess if no clinical improvement. NOTE: Atorvastatin start DEFERRED until azithromycin course complete to avoid macrolide-statin DDI.
heparin: VTE prophylaxis during hospitalization Contingency: Prophylactic dose only (5000 units SQ Q8H). Monitor CBC daily for HIT (platelet count). Hold if active bleeding, platelet count <100K, or if transitioned to therapeutic anticoagulation. Note: patient on concurrent DAPT — monitor for bleeding signs (stool guaiac, hemoglobin).
docusate sodium: Bowel regimen
multivitamin: Nutritional supplementation

gdmt.detail:
atorvastatin: High-intensity statin for secondary prevention of CAD with in-stent restenosis Contingency: DO NOT initiate until azithromycin is discontinued (macrolide + statin → rhabdomyolysis risk). Start day after last azithromycin dose. Check LFTs and CK at baseline and 4-12 weeks. Hold if LFTs >3x ULN or rhabdomyolysis symptoms.
pantoprazole: GI prophylaxis with concurrent DAPT and systemic corticosteroids Contingency: Reassess need after steroid taper; may continue if on long-term DAPT. Selected over omeprazole to avoid CYP2C19 interaction with clopidogrel.

monitor.detail: Macrolide-statin DDI: azithromycin (5-day course) + atorvastatin (new start) → risk of rhabdomyolysis. Atorvastatin initiation deferred until the day after azithromycin course is completed. No concurrent administration.

AGS Beers criteria (age 78): central alpha-agonists associated with CNS adverse effects, orthostatic hypotension, and bradycardia in elderly. Continued to prevent rebound hypertension but taper plan reinforced with explicit schedule (reduce 0.1 mg/week). Monitor orthostatics and mental status.

Losartan (ARB) + furosemide + CKD stage 3b (eGFR 47) + borderline hyperkalemia (K 4.9): risk of AKI and hyperkalemia. Added daily BMP monitoring while inpatient. Hold thresholds explicit in contingency.

Prophylactic heparin SQ + DAPT (aspirin + clopidogrel): additive bleeding risk. Added explicit monitoring for bleeding signs (CBC daily, stool guaiac, hemoglobin trend) and HIT surveillance (platelet count).

No formal TTE available at receiving institution. LVEF is the single most critical unknown — determines HF phenotype (HFrEF vs HFpEF), distinguishes high-gradient from low-flow low-gradient severe AS, guides GDMT eligibility, and informs TAVR surgical risk assessment. Also need diastolic function grading, RV function, and confirmation of AS severity.
Baseline BNP/NT-proBNP not measured. Needed for HF diagnosis confirmation, prognostic stratification, and baseline for monitoring response to therapy and post-TAVR outcomes.
Exclude thyrotoxicosis as contributor to high-output state that could exaggerate AS gradient. Also standard workup in new HF presentation per AHA/ACC guidelines.

Iron deficiency screening in HF (Hgb 12.2 — borderline low for male). Iron deficiency common in HF and independently worsens outcomes. IV iron indicated if ferritin <100 or ferritin 100-300 with TSAT <20%.

stem.presentation: 46-year-old man with metastatic melanoma (BRAF V600E) s/p radiation to spinal metastases, on vemurafenib, and T8 compression fracture s/p 11 rounds of XRT (TLSO brace; outpatient kyphoplasty offered). Recently admitted for chest pain: CTA showed new LLL consolidation, no PE; discharged with a diagnosis of pericarditis and 7-day course of cefpodoxime/azithromycin for presumed aspiration pneumonia. After 5 days at home, symptoms recurred; at 4:30 AM acute substernal pleuritic chest pain, similar to prior, worse sitting, better lying down, with shortness of breath, inability to take deep breaths, and slight leg edema over 3 days; denies orthopnea, PND, dizziness, syncope, fever. ED CT: small to moderate pericardial effusion, increased from last CT. Cardiology: no tamponade or hemodynamic instability; recommended NSAIDs and colchicine. Given IV vancomycin/cefepime/metronidazole for progressing multifocal infiltrates, IV ketorolac, and 3 mg IV morphine total. On the floor, in distress with shallow breathing; describes pressure-like pain.

HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype not applicable (confidence high); etiology not applicable (confidence high).

causes.text: COMPLICATIONS: Hemopericardium, not elsewhere classified (pericardial effusion); Pleural effusion, not elsewhere classified; Bradycardia, unspecified / Tachycardia, unspecified (sinus tachycardia).

CONTRIBUTORS: Malignant melanoma of skin of trunk (metastatic melanoma, BRAF V600E); Pneumonia, unspecified organism; Aspiration pneumonitis due to food and vomit; Adverse effect of antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs, initial encounter.

COMORBIDITIES: Secondary malignant neoplasm of bone; Secondary malignant neoplasm of unspecified lung; Collapsed vertebra, not elsewhere classified, sacral and sacrococcygeal region (pathologic compression fracture); Other chronic pain; Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified; Anxiety disorder, unspecified; Gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis.

acute.text: CONTINUE: hydromorphone IV q3-4h PRN; ondansetron 4 mg IV q6h PRN.
acute.detail:
hydromorphone: Breakthrough pain — pericarditis and metastatic bone pain Contingency: Hold if RR <10 or excessive sedation. Transition to PO when tolerating oral intake. FDA black box warning: concurrent use with benzodiazepine (clonazepam) increases risk of respiratory depression. Continuous pulse oximetry recommended.
ondansetron: Nausea — opioid and/or vemurafenib related Contingency: Monitor QTc closely — additive QT prolongation with vemurafenib, citalopram, and verapamil. Obtain baseline and serial ECGs. Switch to alternative antiemetic (e.g., prochlorperazine, trimethobenzamide) if QTc >500 ms.

acute.text: START: vancomycin IV per pharmacy protocol; cefepime 2000 mg IV q8h; metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h.
acute.detail:
vancomycin: Empiric coverage for multifocal pulmonary consolidations in immunocompromised host Contingency: Monitor trough levels. De-escalate based on culture data.
cefepime: Empiric gram-negative coverage for pulmonary consolidations Contingency: Adjust for renal function. De-escalate based on culture data.
metronidazole: Anaerobic coverage for suspected aspiration pneumonia Contingency: Reassess need at 48-72 hours. Discontinue if no anaerobic source identified.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: ibuprofen 600 mg PO TID; colchicine 0.5 mg PO daily; omeprazole 20 mg PO daily; verapamil PO daily; citalopram PO daily; oxycodone extended-release PO BID; clonazepam PO BID; vemurafenib PO BID; heparin 5000 units SQ q8h; docusate sodium 100 mg PO BID; senna 8.6 mg PO BID; polyethylene glycol 17 g PO daily; aluminum-magnesium hydroxide-simethicone PO PRN.
gdmt.detail:
ibuprofen: Recurrent pericarditis — first-line anti-inflammatory Contingency: Hold if eGFR <30, GI bleeding, or acute kidney injury. Taper gradually — do not stop abruptly. Do NOT administer concurrently with ketorolac.
colchicine: Recurrent pericarditis — adjunctive anti-inflammatory to reduce recurrence Contingency: DOSE REDUCED from 0.5 mg BID to 0.5 mg DAILY due to concurrent verapamil (P-glycoprotein inhibitor) which significantly increases colchicine levels and risk of toxicity. Reduce further or hold if eGFR <30 or severe diarrhea. Monitor for colchicine toxicity (myopathy, cytopenias, diarrhea).
omeprazole: GI prophylaxis during NSAID use Contingency: Appropriate for GI prophylaxis with high-dose NSAID. Reassess need when NSAID discontinued.
verapamil: Home medication — rate control or other indication Contingency: Hold if SBP <90 or HR <50. Note: P-gp/CYP3A4 inhibitor — interacts with colchicine (dose reduced) and may increase vemurafenib levels. Coordinate with oncology. Monitor QTc.
citalopram: Depression/anxiety Contingency: QTc-prolonging agent. Monitor QTc in combination with vemurafenib and ondansetron. Hold or switch to sertraline if QTc >500 ms.
oxycodone extended-release: Chronic cancer-related pain — metastatic osseous disease, T8 compression fracture Contingency: Hold if RR <10 or excessive sedation. FDA black box warning: concurrent use with benzodiazepine (clonazepam) increases risk of respiratory depression and death. Use lowest effective doses. Continuous pulse oximetry recommended.
clonazepam: Anxiety Contingency: FDA black box warning: concurrent use with opioids (oxycodone ER, hydromorphone) increases risk of respiratory depression and death. Monitor sedation, RR, and SpO2 closely. Use lowest effective dose. Evaluate for taper if clinically feasible.
vemurafenib: BRAF V600E metastatic melanoma Contingency: Discuss with oncology re: potential contribution to pericarditis. Consider holding if pericarditis refractory or effusion progresses. Monitor QTc (additive prolongation with citalopram, ondansetron, verapamil). Note: verapamil (CYP3A4 inhibitor) may increase vemurafenib levels — coordinate with oncology for dose adjustment.
heparin: VTE prophylaxis — active malignancy, reduced mobility Contingency: Hold if active bleeding or platelet count <50,000
docusate sodium: Opioid-induced constipation prophylaxis
senna: Opioid-induced constipation prophylaxis
polyethylene glycol: Opioid-induced constipation
aluminum-magnesium hydroxide-simethicone: GI symptom relief Contingency: Separate from colchicine by 2 hours. Separate from cefepime PO (if transitioned) by 2 hours.

monitor.detail: Dual NSAID therapy: ketorolac 30 mg IV q6h concurrent with ibuprofen 600 mg TID provides no additional anti-inflammatory benefit and substantially increases risk of GI hemorrhage, nephrotoxicity, and platelet dysfunction. High-dose ibuprofen is the guideline-recommended first-line NSAID for pericarditis. If oral ibuprofen is not tolerated, IV ketorolac may be substituted (not added).

Verapamil is a potent P-glycoprotein inhibitor that significantly increases colchicine bioavailability, raising risk of life-threatening colchicine toxicity (bone marrow suppression, rhabdomyolysis, multiorgan failure). Dose reduced from 0.5 mg BID to 0.5 mg daily per FDA labeling for concurrent P-gp inhibitor use.

Triple QTc-prolonging combination: citalopram + vemurafenib + ondansetron (with verapamil as additional contributor). Obtain baseline ECG and monitor QTc at 48-72h and with any dose changes. Discontinue ondansetron or switch citalopram to sertraline if QTc >500 ms.

FDA black box warning: concurrent benzodiazepine + opioid (oxycodone ER and hydromorphone) use increases risk of profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death. Continuous pulse oximetry and respiratory rate monitoring required. Evaluate for benzodiazepine taper if clinically feasible.

Verapamil (CYP3A4 inhibitor) may increase vemurafenib plasma levels, potentiating QTc prolongation and other toxicities. Coordinate with oncology for potential dose adjustment. Serial QTc monitoring required.
Diffuse ST elevation with chest pain — need to rule out myopericarditis (troponin elevation would indicate myocardial involvement and change prognosis/monitoring intensity)
Baseline BNP to confirm absence of heart failure and establish reference for serial monitoring given increasing pericardial effusion
Serial ECGs needed for QTc monitoring given 4 concurrent QT-prolonging agents (vemurafenib, citalopram, ondansetron, verapamil) and to track pericarditis evolution
Vemurafenib can cause thyroid dysfunction; sinus tachycardia may have thyroid contribution; baseline TSH warranted

stem.presentation: 69-year-old man with hypertension, aortic stenosis (valve area 1.0-1.2), atrial fibrillation and ESRD on hemodialysis, presenting from dialysis with acute chest pain after the session and HR 150 that broke spontaneously. Prior post-surgical AF was cardioverted and treated with amiodarone and warfarin, later discontinued; follow-up Holters showed sinus rhythm. Pain was nonradiating, "like food is stuck in my chest," without dyspnea or palpitations. Received aspirin before arrival; chest pain free in ED. Rectal: guaiac-positive stool, no gross blood. At ~22:30 HR rose to 150s (thought AF with aberrancy) with chest pain, dyspnea and palpitations; received metoprolol 100 mg PO and 35 mg IV total plus diltiazem 10 mg IV; HR improved to low 100s in AF, then sinus. Heparin drip not started given guaiac-positive stool. Received ~1.5 L IV NS. On floor arrival, RR 30 with dyspnea and crackles; given furosemide 80 mg IV and ipratropium-albuterol nebs with improvement.
stem.home_meds: From first-12 h orders: no maintenance-type medications; only albuterol 0.083% neb, ipratropium bromide neb and furosemide 80 mg IV were ordered. Home medications not listed in the note (amiodarone and warfarin previously discontinued).

Floor arrival: T 98, HR 77, BP 187/95, RR 28 (triggered for RR 30), SpO2 91% on 4 L; after furosemide/nebs: HR 77, BP 143/70, RR 20, SpO2 96% on 4 L.

HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype HFpEF (confidence high); etiology hypertensive (confidence moderate).

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Unspecified atrial fibrillation (paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response); Nonrheumatic aortic (valve) stenosis; Anemia, unspecified.

COMPLICATIONS: ST elevation myocardial infarction of unspecified site — Type 2 myocardial infarction (demand ischemia); Primary pulmonary hypertension — Pulmonary hypertension secondary to left heart disease (Group 2); Gastrointestinal hemorrhage, unspecified; Acute pulmonary edema.

COMORBIDITIES: End-stage renal disease; Dependence on renal dialysis; Essential (primary) hypertension; Nonrheumatic aortic (valve) insufficiency — Mild mitral regurgitation; Cardiomegaly; Hypokalemia — Electrolyte monitoring in ESRD; Ventricular fibrillation — Prolonged QT interval.

acute.text: CONTINUE: furosemide 80 mg IV once.
acute.detail: furosemide: Acute decompensated HFpEF with pulmonary edema — bridge to HD ultrafiltration Contingency: Transition volume management to HD ultrafiltration. Discontinue IV furosemide once HD ultrafiltration plan optimized. Oral furosemide only if residual urine output >200 mL/day. Note: with eGFR 16.9, diuretic response may be minimal; HD ultrafiltration is primary volume removal strategy.

acute.text: START: pantoprazole 40 mg IV daily.
acute.detail: pantoprazole: GI prophylaxis given guaiac-positive stool, anemia, and anticipated anticoagulation Contingency: Transition to PO 40mg daily when tolerating oral intake. Continue at least through GI evaluation. Continue long-term if anticoagulation started (GI protection indication present). Reassess annually for continued need.

acute.text: START (conditional — see details): epoetin-alfa IV per HD protocol (typically 3x/week with dialysis).
acute.detail: epoetin-alfa: Anemia of ESRD contributing to demand ischemia and HF decompensation (Hgb 9.4) Contingency: Check iron studies first; replete iron if TSAT <20% or ferritin <200. Target Hgb 10-11 g/dL, do NOT exceed 11. Hold if Hgb >11 or uncontrolled hypertension. Defer if active GI bleeding — transfuse PRBCs instead.

gdmt.text: START: metoprolol-succinate 50 mg PO daily; aspirin 81 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
metoprolol-succinate: Rate control for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; heart rate management in HFpEF Contingency: Hold if HR <55 or SBP <90. Uptitrate to 100-200mg daily if resting HR >110 in AF or >80 in sinus. Avoid IV diltiazem long-term.
aspirin: Secondary cardiovascular prevention given moderate AS, type 2 MI, atherosclerotic risk Contingency: Hold if active GI bleeding confirmed. SAFETY NOTE: If warfarin is initiated, combination aspirin + warfarin increases bleeding risk significantly. Reassess need — discontinue aspirin unless compelling indication (e.g., recent ACS/PCI within 12 months). If both continued, monitor CBC and stool guaiac weekly; ensure PPI co-therapy. Resume after GI clearance.
atorvastatin: Cardiovascular risk reduction given calcific AS, type 2 MI, atherosclerotic risk profile Contingency: Monitor LFTs at baseline and 4-12 weeks. Discontinue if myopathy or hepatotoxicity. Shared decision-making given uncertain benefit in dialysis population (AURORA/4D trials showed no benefit for statins initiated in dialysis patients — discuss with patient).

gdmt.text: HOLD: warfarin PO daily; amiodarone PO N/A.
gdmt.detail:
warfarin: Stroke prevention in paroxysmal AF with CHA2DS2-VASc ≥4; ESRD precludes DOAC use Contingency: HOLD until GI evaluation (EGD ± colonoscopy) completed and active bleeding excluded. If no high-risk lesion, initiate warfarin with INR target 2.0-3.0. Recheck INR 2-3x/week during initiation. If active bleeding found, defer anticoagulation and reassess risk-benefit with multidisciplinary team. SAFETY NOTE: If aspirin 81mg is continued concurrently, monitor for bleeding signs daily and reassess combination need at each visit — minimize dual antithrombotic duration unless compelling indication. SAFETY NOTE: If amiodarone is restarted, reduce warfarin dose by 30-50% and monitor INR every 3 days until stable.
amiodarone: Previously discontinued; was used post-cardioversion in past Contingency: Consider restarting only if recurrent symptomatic AF despite adequate rate control with metoprolol, and rhythm control strategy is pursued. Requires thyroid and pulmonary monitoring. Discuss with electrophysiology. SAFETY NOTE: If restarted AND warfarin is active, reduce warfarin dose by 30-50% and monitor INR every 3 days until stable (amiodarone-warfarin DDI — major).

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: albuterol 2.5 mg nebulizer Q4H PRN; ipratropium 0.5 mg nebulizer Q6H PRN.
gdmt.detail:
albuterol: Bronchospasm/dyspnea symptom relief Contingency: Wean as respiratory status improves. Monitor for tachycardia given AF history. Monitor potassium — albuterol causes intracellular K+ shift; coordinate with HD electrolyte management.
ipratropium: Bronchospasm/dyspnea symptom relief (home medication) Contingency: Wean as respiratory status improves.

monitor.detail: Concurrent aspirin 81mg and warfarin (when initiated) constitutes dual antithrombotic therapy with increased bleeding risk, especially given guaiac-positive stool and anemia (Hgb 9.4). Added monitoring language: weekly CBC, stool guaiac, and explicit instruction to discontinue aspirin unless compelling indication persists. PPI co-therapy mandatory.

Amiodarone is currently held but contingency allows restart. Amiodarone + warfarin is a major DDI causing INR elevation and bleeding risk. Added safety note to both warfarin and amiodarone contingencies: if amiodarone restarted, reduce warfarin 30-50% and monitor INR every 3 days until stable.

Already marked as discontinue in proposed list. Confirming removal from active curated prescriptions. While HFpEF (not HFrEF) does not absolutely contraindicate non-DHP CCBs, the admitting team already discontinued it in favor of metoprolol succinate for rate control, which is appropriate given the HF context and concurrent aortic stenosis. Single-dose IV rescue noted in metoprolol contingency if needed.
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) needed before initiating ESA therapy for anemia of ESRD. Must distinguish iron deficiency anemia from anemia of chronic disease and GI blood loss.

Thyroid function assessment needed: (1) AF can be precipitated by hyperthyroidism, (2) amiodarone was previously used (thyroid toxicity risk), (3) baseline before potential amiodarone re-initiation for rhythm control.
Serial troponins q8h x3 to confirm downtrending pattern consistent with type 2 MI rather than evolving type 1 ACS. Current troponin 0.14 is plateau — need to confirm decline.

stem.presentation: 66-year-old woman who underwent a complicated anterior cervical fusion with neurosurgery for a cervical disc herniation after a fall (right digit and lateral forearm numbness) and was discharged yesterday; she must remain in a hard collar for another month. She awoke at 4 am with substernal, non-radiating chest pain worsened by cough, cough productive of a large amount of phlegm, and persistent palpitations; she also reports increased shortness of breath today. She denies fever, chills, leg swelling, and difficulty swallowing. In the ED, HR was 160; she received 1 L IV fluid, a total of 50 mg diltiazem plus 30 mg PO diltiazem, and ceftriaxone, azithromycin, and vancomycin for reported phlegm. CTA showed post-surgical changes including pneumomediastinum (neurosurgery: expected). ENT laryngoscopy showed vocal cord paralysis; NPO and speech/swallow evaluation were recommended. gdmt.detail:
apixaban: Stroke prevention in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, CHA₂DS₂-VASc 2, TEE with spontaneous echo contrast Contingency: Hold if active bleeding, platelet count <50K, or prior to invasive procedures. TRANSITION: First apixaban dose to be given 6 hours AFTER heparin drip is discontinued. Do NOT administer concurrently with heparin.
amiodarone: Rhythm control for paroxysmal AF with tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy; post-cardioversion maintenance Contingency: Hold if QTc >500 ms, HR <50, or significant hepatotoxicity (ALT >3x ULN). Plan to discontinue after successful catheter ablation. Monitor LFTs at baseline, 1 month, then q3 months. Monitor TFTs q6 months. Obtain baseline PFTs.
metoprolol succinate: Rate control for paroxysmal AF; cardioprotection during Takotsubo recovery Contingency: Hold if SBP <90 or HR <55. Uptitrate to 50 mg daily after 1-2 weeks if tolerated.
potassium chloride: Hypokalemia (K 3.3) from diuresis; maintain K ≥4.0 for arrhythmia prevention Contingency: Reduce to 20 mEq daily once K ≥4.0. Discontinue if K >5.0 or furosemide discontinued. Note: lisinopril may raise K — monitor BMP q2-3d during co-administration.
magnesium oxide: Magnesium repletion to support potassium repletion and reduce AF recurrence Contingency: Discontinue if diarrhea develops; switch to magnesium glycinate if GI intolerance
lisinopril: Neurohormonal modulation for Takotsubo cardiomyopathy with residual apical hypokinesis; afterload reduction Contingency: Hold if SBP <90, K >5.5, or Cr rises >30% from baseline. Uptitrate to 5-10 mg daily as BP permits.
dapagliflozin: HFpEF GDMT — SGLT2 inhibitor (Class I recommendation) Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20, recurrent UTIs/genital mycotic infections, or signs of DKA. Counsel on genital hygiene. SAFETY NOTE: Triple combination with furosemide + lisinopril increases AKI risk during initiation — monitor BMP and renal function (Cr, eGFR, K) every 3 days for the first 2 weeks of co-initiation. Hold dapagliflozin if Cr rises >30% from baseline or signs of volume depletion.

dapagliflozin: HFrEF LVEF 22% — GDMT Pillar 4 (SGLT2 inhibitor) Contingency: Hold if recurrent UTI or genital mycotic infections; no dose adjustment for renal function at eGFR 115. SAFETY NOTE: SGLT2i + loop diuretic (furosemide) + RAAS inhibitor (sacubitril-valsartan) — monitor BMP and renal function (Cr, eGFR, K+) at 3 days and 1 week after initiation; hold if Cr rises >30% from baseline or signs of hypovolemia.
apixaban: Anticoagulation for AF with CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (CHF + HTN); DOAC preferred over warfarin Contingency: Reduce to 2.5 mg BID only if ≥2 of: age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, Cr ≥1.5 (none currently met); hold for active bleeding. TRANSITION: Do NOT administer first dose until heparin drip has been discontinued for ≥6 hours. See heparin discontinuation order.

gdmt.detail:
metoprolol tartrate: Non-evidence-based beta-blocker formulation for HFrEF — replacing with carvedilol Contingency: Discontinue upon initiation of carvedilol
aspirin: No indication for aspirin in AF without ACS/CAD — given once in ED, do not continue Contingency: Restart only if coronary evaluation reveals obstructive CAD; concurrent aspirin + DOAC increases bleeding risk without benefit in AF alone

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: amiodarone 200 mg PO TID; amlodipine 5 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily; sertraline PO daily; pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily; cholecalciferol PO daily; fluticasone propionate nasal nasal daily.
gdmt.detail:
amiodarone: Rhythm control for new-onset AF in setting of HFrEF; tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy Contingency: Monitor QTc — hold if QTc >500 ms; transition to 200 mg daily maintenance after loading; monitor LFTs and TFTs q6 months; reassess need if EF recovers. SAFETY NOTE: Amiodarone increases statin exposure (CYP3A4 inhibition) — see atorvastatin note. Additive bradycardia with carvedilol — see carvedilol note. Additive QTc prolongation with sertraline — obtain baseline EKG and repeat in 48-72h.
amlodipine: Hypertension — safe in HFrEF (DHP CCB) but no HF benefit; bridge BP control during GDMT initiation Contingency: Discontinue once sacubitril/valsartan and carvedilol uptitrated and BP controlled; hold if SBP <100
atorvastatin: Cardiovascular risk reduction — continue home medication Contingency: SAFETY NOTE: Amiodarone inhibits CYP3A4 and increases atorvastatin exposure. Monitor for myalgias, muscle weakness; check CK if symptomatic. Consider reducing to 20 mg if myopathy symptoms develop. Atorvastatin 40 mg is acceptable (risk is highest with simvastatin/lovastatin); do NOT exceed 40 mg while on amiodarone.
sertraline: Psychiatric indication — safe in HFrEF (SADHART trial) Contingency: SAFETY NOTE: Additive QTc prolongation with amiodarone. Obtain baseline EKG and repeat at 48-72h; hold if QTc >500 ms. Monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms.
pantoprazole: GERD / GI protection on anticoagulation Contingency: Reassess need at outpatient follow-up; monitor magnesium. Pantoprazole is the preferred PPI (no interaction with clopidogrel, though clopidogrel not currently prescribed).
cholecalciferol: Vitamin D supplementation — continue home medication
fluticasone propionate nasal: Allergic rhinitis — continue home medication

monitor.detail: Dual anticoagulation hazard: heparin + apixaban overlap causes bleeding. Original order stated 'discontinue after first dose of apixaban' which implies concurrent administration. CORRECTED: heparin drip must be stopped ≥6 hours BEFORE first apixaban dose. Apixaban transition language also updated.
Linked to heparin transition correction. Added explicit instruction: do not administer first apixaban dose until heparin has been off for ≥6 hours.

Amiodarone (CYP3A4 inhibitor) + atorvastatin 40 mg increases rhabdomyolysis risk. Atorvastatin is less affected than simvastatin/lovastatin and 40 mg is within acceptable range, but monitoring for myopathy symptoms and CK if symptomatic is required. Do not exceed 40 mg.
Amiodarone + carvedilol: additive bradycardia and AV block risk. Added EKG and HR monitoring within 48h of initiation and after each dose titration.
Amiodarone + sertraline: additive QTc prolongation. Added baseline EKG and repeat at 48-72h; hold threshold QTc >500 ms.
SGLT2i + loop diuretic (furosemide) + RAAS inhibitor (sacubitril-valsartan) — triple combination increases AKI risk during initiation. Added renal function monitoring at 3 days and 1 week.

Cardiac MRI with LGE and T1 mapping to evaluate for myocarditis (preceding viral illness, acute biventricular dysfunction), fibrosis pattern, and to definitively characterize etiology (tachycardia-mediated vs myocarditis vs early DCM). Critical if LVEF does not recover at 3 months.
BNP/NT-proBNP was not measured during this admission. Needed for baseline risk stratification in new HFrEF and to track trajectory with GDMT initiation.
Troponin not documented. Needed to rule out ACS given ST-T wave changes on ECG and to assess for myocarditis (elevated troponin in acute myocarditis). Critical for differential diagnosis.

Coronary evaluation (invasive angiography or CT coronary angiography) to definitively exclude ischemic etiology of cardiomyopathy. ST-T changes on ECG warrant coronary assessment despite global hypokinesis pattern.
Iron studies recommended in all new HFrEF patients per guidelines. Iron deficiency (even without anemia) is common in HF and treatable with IV iron to improve functional capacity.
