dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Decompensated Heart Failure secondary to Tachycardia-Mediated Cardiomyopathy from Thyrotoxicosis (HFimpEF) (confidence high).
HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype HFrEF (confidence high); etiology tachycardia mediated (confidence high).

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy; Thyrotoxicosis, unspecified, without thyrotoxic crisis or storm; Unspecified atrial fibrillation.

COMORBIDITIES: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris; Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, unspecified; Ventricular premature complexes; Pulmonary hypertension, unspecified; Anemia, unspecified; Abnormal weight loss; Other specified symptoms and signs involving the circulatory and respiratory systems (pulmonary nodules); Gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis.
COMPLICATIONS: Stenosis of coronary artery stent, initial encounter; Hypokalemia.
HISTORY: Nicotine dependence, cigarettes, uncomplicated.

acute.text: CONTINUE: furosemide 40 mg IV BID (acute phase), then transition to PO 20-40 mg daily; magnesium sulfate IV per protocol.
acute.detail:
furosemide: Volume overload — pulmonary edema, BNP 11,590 Contingency: Target UOP >0.5 mL/kg/hr. Transition to PO when euvolemic. May discontinue outpatient if euvolemia maintained after euthyroidism achieved. Replete K and Mg with each dose. Monitor BMP q3d given concurrent SGLT2i and sacubitril-valsartan initiation.
magnesium sulfate: Hypomagnesemia repletion to support potassium repletion and reduce arrhythmia risk Contingency: Transition to oral magnesium oxide 400 mg daily at discharge. Target Mg >2.0.

acute.text: STOP: heparin IV per protocol.
acute.detail: heparin: Bridge anticoagulation for AF Contingency: MANDATORY TRANSITION: Stop heparin drip at least 6 hours BEFORE first dose of apixaban. Do NOT co-administer. Confirm aPTT trending down before apixaban initiation. First apixaban dose should be given ≥6h after heparin discontinuation.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: propranolol PO TID or QID per current regimen; methimazole 20 mg PO daily; ipratropium bromide 0.5 mg INH Q6H PRN; potassium chloride 40 mEq PO daily (adjust per levels); acetaminophen 650 mg PO Q6H PRN.
gdmt.detail:
propranolol: Rate control for AF, thyrotoxicosis symptom management, prevention of tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy recurrence Contingency: Hold if HR <50 or SBP <90. Monitor for bronchospasm given COPD. Consider switch to metoprolol succinate if respiratory symptoms worsen.
methimazole: Thyrotoxicosis — primary driver of tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy Contingency: Monitor TSH/free T4 every 4-6 weeks. Check CBC for agranulocytosis. Adjust dose to achieve euthyroidism.
ipratropium bromide: COPD maintenance/rescue bronchodilation Contingency: Preferred over beta-agonists given tachycardia history.
potassium chloride: Hypokalemia repletion — target K >4.0 given QT prolongation and PVC burden Contingency: Reduce or hold if K >5.0. SAFETY NOTE: Patient is on sacubitril-valsartan + spironolactone — monitor K closely (BMP q3d). Anticipate reducing and discontinuing KCl as spironolactone is uptitrated. Do NOT continue KCl if K ≥4.5 once spironolactone is at 25 mg daily.
acetaminophen: Analgesia/antipyretic Contingency: Max 3g/day. Preferred analgesic — avoid NSAIDs.

gdmt.text: START: sacubitril-valsartan 24 mg PO BID; spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily; dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily; apixaban 5 mg PO BID; clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily; aspirin 81 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily; pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
sacubitril-valsartan: HFimpEF (prior LVEF 28%, now ≥75%) — GDMT pillar 1 Contingency: Hold if SBP <100 or K >5.5. Uptitrate to 49/51 mg BID then 97/103 mg BID every 2 weeks as tolerated. Monitor BMP q3d during initiation given concurrent SGLT2i + loop diuretic (triple nephrotoxic risk).
spironolactone: HFimpEF — GDMT pillar 3. Also beneficial for hypokalemia tendency. Contingency: Hold if K >5.5 or eGFR <30. Uptitrate to 25 mg daily if K remains <5.0 and Cr stable. Check BMP at 3 days and 7 days after initiation. Reassess need for potassium chloride supplementation once spironolactone is at target dose — anticipate discontinuing KCl to avoid hyperkalemia.
dapagliflozin: HFimpEF — GDMT pillar 4 Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20. Monitor for volume depletion, UTI, genital mycotic infections. Adjust diuretic if needed. SAFETY NOTE: SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ARB (sacubitril-valsartan) — monitor renal function (BMP) every 3 days during initiation phase for AKI risk.
apixaban: Anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation (CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥3) and post-PCI dual pathway therapy Contingency: Reduce to 2.5 mg BID if 2 of 3: age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, Cr ≥1.5. Hold if active major bleeding. Monitor Hgb given baseline anemia (10.4). Coordinate with hem/onc if malignancy confirmed. TRANSITION: Do NOT administer first dose until heparin drip has been discontinued for ≥6 hours. Confirm patient tolerating PO before starting.
clopidogrel: DAPT after DES placement for in-stent restenosis of proximal LCx Contingency: Continue for minimum 6 months, ideally 12 months. May shorten to 3-6 months if high bleeding risk. Discontinue aspirin after 1 week — continue clopidogrel + apixaban as dual pathway therapy. NOTE: Omeprazole switched to pantoprazole to avoid CYP2C19 interaction.
aspirin: Short-term triple therapy post-PCI with DES in setting of concurrent anticoagulation for AF Contingency: Discontinue after 7 days to reduce bleeding risk. Continue dual pathway therapy (apixaban + clopidogrel) thereafter. Monitor for GI bleeding — check Hgb daily during triple therapy given baseline anemia (10.4). PPI (pantoprazole) in place for GI prophylaxis.
atorvastatin: High-intensity statin for secondary prevention post-PCI, CAD with in-stent restenosis Contingency: Monitor LFTs at 6-12 weeks. Reduce dose if transaminases >3x ULN or myopathy symptoms.
pantoprazole: GI prophylaxis with concurrent anticoagulation + antiplatelet therapy Contingency: Switched from omeprazole to pantoprazole to avoid CYP2C19 inhibition reducing clopidogrel efficacy. Reassess need when antithrombotic therapy is de-escalated. Avoid long-term use beyond antithrombotic indication per Beers criteria.

monitor.detail: Clopidogrel + omeprazole is a major DDI: omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 and reduces clopidogrel's antiplatelet efficacy. Switched to pantoprazole 40 mg daily, which has minimal CYP2C19 interaction. GI prophylaxis indication is valid given triple antithrombotic therapy.

Heparin + apixaban concurrent administration causes bleeding. Enforced explicit transition: heparin drip must be stopped ≥6 hours before first apixaban dose. Added aPTT check and explicit timing language to contingency.

ACEi/ARB (sacubitril-valsartan) + spironolactone + KCl supplementation → hyperkalemia risk. Currently justified by K 3.6 and active diuresis, but requires aggressive monitoring (BMP q3d) and explicit discontinuation plan as spironolactone is uptitrated. KCl should be stopped once K ≥4.5 on stable spironolactone dose.
SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ARB component (sacubitril-valsartan) constitutes a triple nephrotoxic combination with AKI risk. Added renal function monitoring every 3 days during initiation phase.

Triple antithrombotic therapy (aspirin + clopidogrel + apixaban) for 7 days post-PCI. Duration is within ≤30-day guideline limit. Added daily Hgb monitoring during triple therapy given baseline anemia (Hgb 10.4) and active hem/onc workup.

Thyrotoxicosis is the root cause of tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy. TSH and free T4/T3 levels needed to quantify severity and guide methimazole titration. Not documented as drawn at this facility.
Extensive ST-T changes on ECG with known CAD and in-stent restenosis. Need serial troponins to definitively exclude acute myocardial injury as a contributing factor to the presentation.

Anemia (Hgb 10.4) with 30-lb weight loss — iron studies including ferritin needed to characterize anemia (iron deficiency vs. anemia of chronic disease vs. malignancy-related) and assess for iron deficiency which independently worsens HF outcomes.
Repeat BNP/NT-proBNP at this facility to track trajectory after diuresis and rate control. Initial BNP 11,590 at OSH — trend needed to confirm response to therapy and establish discharge baseline.
Discharge ECG to document rhythm (sinus vs AF), QT interval after electrolyte correction, and ST-T changes at baseline for future comparison.

acute.text: START: furosemide 40 mg IV BID.
acute.detail: furosemide: Acute decompensated HFpEF — decongestion (pulmonary vascular congestion on CXR, weight above dry weight, orthopnea, PND) Contingency: Titrate to UOP >0.5 mL/kg/hr; hold if SBP <90 or Cr rises >50% from baseline; monitor K, Mg, Na q8-12h during active diuresis. SAFETY NOTE: Part of SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ACEi triad — monitor renal function q3d.

acute.detail: furosemide: Maintenance diuresis for HFpEF — prevent recurrent congestion Contingency: Transition from IV once euvolemic (at dry weight ~77 kg); adjust dose based on daily weights and symptoms; hold if SBP <90 or signs of over-diuresis

gdmt.text: START: dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily; lisinopril 5 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 80 mg PO daily; aspirin 81 mg PO daily; spironolactone 25 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
dapagliflozin: HFpEF — reduce HF hospitalization and CV death; DM2 glycemic and renal benefit Contingency: Hold if eGFR <20; monitor for genital mycotic infections; hold if signs of euglycemic DKA. SAFETY NOTE: Being initiated concurrently with loop diuretic (furosemide) and ACEi (lisinopril) — monitor BMP and renal function q3d during initiation phase to mitigate AKI risk from SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ACEi combination.
lisinopril: HTN (uncontrolled SBP 140-150), CAD secondary prevention, DM2 renal protection, HFpEF (Class 2b for hospitalization reduction) Contingency: Hold if K >5.5, eGFR <20, or SBP <90; check BMP within 1-2 weeks; uptitrate to 20-40 mg as tolerated. SAFETY NOTE: Concurrent with spironolactone — do NOT add potassium supplements without documented hypokalemia. Monitor K closely q3-5d during co-initiation of ACEi + MRA. Also part of SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ACEi triad — monitor renal function q3d during initiation.
atorvastatin: High-intensity statin for CAD secondary prevention, DM2, HLD Contingency: Monitor LFTs at 4-12 weeks; reduce to 40 mg if myalgias or LFT >3x ULN
aspirin: CAD secondary prevention s/p CABG Contingency: If paroxysmal AF confirmed with CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥2 (which this patient meets), transition to DOAC and reassess need for concurrent aspirin vs. anticoagulation alone
spironolactone: HFpEF — Class IIb recommendation for MRA to reduce HF hospitalizations Contingency: Hold if K ≥5.0 or eGFR <30; check BMP within 3-5 days of initiation and weekly for first month given concurrent ACEi (lisinopril) initiation. ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to concurrent potassium supplementation — do NOT add K+ supplements unless K <3.5 and with close monitoring. Monitor renal function and potassium q3-5d during co-initiation with lisinopril.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: carvedilol 25 mg PO BID; insulin SQ per home regimen; heparin SQ per protocol.
gdmt.detail:
carvedilol: HTN and CAD rate/BP control; home medication Contingency: Hold if HR <50 or SBP <90; consider dose reduction if symptomatic bradycardia or worsening AV block (patient has baseline first-degree AV block)
insulin: DM2 glycemic management Contingency: Adjust doses with addition of SGLT2i to avoid hypoglycemia; inpatient sliding scale per protocol
heparin: VTE prophylaxis during hospitalization Contingency: Discontinue at discharge unless AF confirmed requiring anticoagulation transition to DOAC. NOTE: This is prophylactic-dose SQ heparin (not therapeutic); no dual-anticoagulation concern at prophylactic dosing. If transitioning to DOAC for AF, stop heparin ≥6h before first DOAC dose.

monitor.detail: ACEi + MRA combination carries hyperkalemia risk (lisinopril + spironolactone). Both are being initiated simultaneously. No baseline potassium available in labs. Added mandatory potassium and renal function monitoring q3-5d during co-initiation. Potassium supplements are explicitly contraindicated unless documented hypokalemia (K <3.5). Per checklist: ACEi + spironolactone + K+ supplement → hyperkalemia; ensuring no K+ supplement is added.

monitor.text: SAFETY ADD MONITORING (moderate): dapagliflozin + furosemide + lisinopril.
monitor.detail: SGLT2i + loop diuretic + ACEi triple combination carries AKI risk per safety checklist. All three are being initiated concurrently in an acutely decompensated patient. Added renal function monitoring q3d during initiation phase. No baseline creatinine/eGFR available — obtaining baseline renal function is critical before starting this combination.

Home heparin continued as prophylactic-dose SQ for VTE prophylaxis — no dual-anticoagulation concern at prophylactic dosing. However, if paroxysmal AF is confirmed on telemetry and a DOAC is initiated, heparin must be stopped ≥6h before first DOAC dose. Added explicit transition language to contingency.

BNP/NT-proBNP not measured. Essential to confirm HFpEF diagnosis per ESC/AHA criteria (NT-proBNP >125 pg/mL in sinus rhythm), establish baseline for monitoring, and strengthen diagnostic confidence given incomplete diastolic assessment on echo.

Not drawn on admission. While ACS is low probability, troponin should be obtained in any acute HF presentation to rule out ischemic precipitant, especially given CAD history and possible old anteroseptal infarct on ECG.

Repeat TTE with comprehensive diastolic function assessment (E/e', LA volume index, TR velocity) and dedicated aortic valve evaluation (gradients, valve area) to resolve the critical discrepancy between documented AS history with systolic murmur and absence of AS on current echo.
Repeat ECG with rhythm strip to clarify machine-read AFib vs physician-read sinus rhythm discrepancy. Continuous telemetry monitoring for paroxysmal AF detection.

stem.presentation: 55-year-old man with severe nonischemic cardiomyopathy, congenital subaortic membrane status post sternotomy and repair twice, and chronic kidney disease, listed as UNOS status 2 for heart-kidney transplant, directly admitted with worsening abdominal edema and weight gain. He recently called the heart failure clinic with weight up to 75 kg (a 5-pound increase from baseline over a 2-week period) and worsening edema. His abdominal edema continued to worsen despite torsemide being increased from 60 mg BID to 80 mg BID. He denies chest pain, increased shortness of breath from baseline, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations, syncope or presyncope. On arrival to the floor he was sitting up in bed and resting comfortably, weight 74.9 kg. Orders in the first 12 h included furosemide 80 mg IV, a furosemide 250 mg IV drip, and metolazone 2.5 mg PO.
stem.home_meds: From first-12 h orders: aspirin 81 mg PO, levothyroxine 112 mcg PO, omeprazole 20 mg PO, isosorbide mononitrate ER 90 mg PO, metoprolol succinate XL 50 mg PO, hydralazine 20 mg PO, spironolactone 25 mg PO, amiodarone 100 mg PO and amiodarone 50 mg PO (two separate orders). HPI: torsemide 80 mg BID.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute on Chronic Systolic (Congestive) Heart Failure — Stage D, NYHA Class III, with Diuretic Resistance and Cardiorenal Syndrome (I50.23) (confidence high).
HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype HFrEF (confidence high); etiology idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (confidence high).

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Dilated cardiomyopathy (nonischemic); Tricuspid insufficiency, severe; Chronic kidney disease, stage 4; Primary pulmonary hypertension; Nonrheumatic mitral valve insufficiency; Nonrheumatic aortic (valve) insufficiency.
HISTORY: Nonrheumatic aortic (valve) stenosis — history of congenital subaortic membrane, status post repair.

COMORBIDITIES: Presence of cardiac pacemaker (CRT-D); Hypothyroidism, unspecified; Anemia, unspecified; Status post heart transplant listing / encounter for transplant evaluation; Gastro-esophageal reflux disease, unspecified.
COMPLICATIONS: Hypo-osmolality and hyponatremia; Ascites (abdominal edema/fluid retention).

acute.text: START: furosemide 160 mg IV bolus then 10-20 mg/hr continuous infusion.
acute.detail: furosemide: Acute decompensated HFrEF with diuretic resistance and volume overload Contingency: Titrate drip rate to UOP >100 mL/hr. Hold if SBP <85 or Cr rises >0.5 from baseline without diuretic response. Consider adding IV chlorothiazide 250-500mg if inadequate response. Monitor BMP q8h given eGFR 28.

acute.text: CONTINUE: metolazone 5 mg PO daily.
acute.detail: metolazone: Sequential nephron blockade for diuretic resistance Contingency: Hold if Na <128 or K <3.0. Give 30 minutes before loop diuretic dose.

acute.text: HOLD: torsemide 80 mg PO BID.
acute.detail: torsemide: Home loop diuretic — held during IV diuresis, resume at discharge Contingency: Hold during IV furosemide infusion. Resume oral torsemide at discharge, dose adjusted based on diuretic response and volume status.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: spironolactone 25 mg PO daily; metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily; hydralazine PO TID; isosorbide mononitrate PO daily; amiodarone 150 mg PO daily; heparin 5000 units SQ TID; levothyroxine PO daily; omeprazole 20 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
spironolactone: HFrEF GDMT — MRA for mortality benefit Contingency: Hold if K >5.0 or eGFR <20. Monitor K q8h during aggressive diuresis. Heightened hyperkalemia risk with eGFR 28 — recheck BMP daily once diuresis stabilizes. No concurrent potassium supplementation without checking K first.
metoprolol succinate: HFrEF GDMT — evidence-based beta-blocker for mortality benefit Contingency: Downtitrate to 25 mg if SBP <90 or HR <55 or signs of low cardiac output. Do not uptitrate during acute decompensation.
hydralazine: HFrEF — vasodilator in lieu of ACEi/ARB/ARNi due to CKD stage 4 Contingency: Hold if SBP <90. Resume/uptitrate once hemodynamically stable.
isosorbide mononitrate: HFrEF — H-ISDN combination in lieu of ACEi/ARB/ARNi due to CKD stage 4 Contingency: Hold if SBP <90 or symptomatic hypotension.
amiodarone: Ventricular arrhythmia suppression in severe nonischemic cardiomyopathy with CRT-D Contingency: Monitor TSH, LFTs q3-6 months. Hold if QTc >500ms or hepatotoxicity. IMPORTANT: amiodarone increases warfarin effect — see warfarin entry for dose reduction and INR monitoring.
heparin: VTE prophylaxis; escalate to therapeutic if LV thrombus confirmed Contingency: If LV thrombus confirmed: (1) escalate to therapeutic IV heparin (target aPTT 60-80s), (2) start warfarin concurrently, (3) discontinue therapeutic heparin ONLY after INR ≥2.0 for ≥24 consecutive hours. If LV thrombus NOT confirmed: continue prophylactic SQ heparin during immobility/hospitalization, discontinue at discharge. Do NOT administer prophylactic SQ heparin concurrently with therapeutic IV heparin — switch, do not overlap.
levothyroxine: Hypothyroidism (possibly amiodarone-induced) Contingency: Check TSH during admission. Adjust dose if TSH out of range. Separate administration by ≥4 hours from omeprazole (PPIs reduce levothyroxine absorption).
omeprazole: GI prophylaxis Contingency: Consider discontinuation if aspirin stopped and no other GI indication. Separate from levothyroxine by ≥4 hours.

gdmt.text: START (conditional — see details): dapagliflozin 10 mg PO daily; warfarin 2.5 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
dapagliflozin: HFrEF GDMT — SGLT2i for mortality and HF hospitalization reduction; additional cardiorenal benefit Contingency: Start once SBP consistently >95 and patient hemodynamically stable. Hold if eGFR <20 or symptomatic hypotension. Monitor BMP and renal function q3d during initiation given eGFR 28 and concurrent loop diuretic + metolazone. Anticipate initial eGFR dip; do not discontinue unless eGFR drops >30% or <20.
warfarin: Anticoagulation for suspected/confirmed LV thrombus in setting of apical dyskinesis with LVEF 22% Contingency: Start only if LV thrombus confirmed on contrast echo or cardiac MRI. DOSE REDUCED from 5 mg to 2.5 mg due to concurrent amiodarone (amiodarone inhibits warfarin metabolism, increasing INR 30-50%). Monitor INR q3d until stable in therapeutic range (target INR 2.0-3.0). Overlap with therapeutic IV heparin until INR ≥2.0 for ≥24h, then discontinue heparin. Minimum 3-6 months if thrombus confirmed, with repeat imaging.

gdmt.text: STOP: aspirin 81 mg PO daily.
gdmt.detail: aspirin: Currently on for unclear indication (nonischemic cardiomyopathy without documented CAD) Contingency: Discontinue once therapeutic anticoagulation with warfarin is established. No documented CAD or ischemic indication. If LV thrombus not confirmed and warfarin not started, may continue pending transplant team input.

monitor.detail: Major DDI: warfarin + amiodarone. Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 and CYP3A4, increasing warfarin effect by 30-50%. Starting dose reduced from 5 mg to 2.5 mg daily. INR monitoring q3d added until stable.

Dual anticoagulation risk: heparin (prophylactic or therapeutic) and warfarin will overlap during bridge. Explicit transition language added: discontinue therapeutic heparin only after INR ≥2.0 for ≥24h. Prophylactic SQ heparin must stop when therapeutic IV heparin starts — no concurrent dosing of two heparin regimens.

SGLT2i initiation with eGFR 28 (CKD stage 4) and concurrent aggressive loop diuretic + metolazone therapy increases AKI risk. Renal function monitoring q3d added during initiation period. Drug is guideline-supported down to eGFR 20 for HFrEF but requires vigilance in this context.

MRA with eGFR 28 (CKD stage 4) poses hyperkalemia risk despite current K 3.5. Aggressive diuresis may transiently protect, but risk rises as diuresis slows. Enhanced potassium monitoring q8h during diuresis, then daily. Hold threshold K >5.0 or eGFR <20.
Concurrent omeprazole reduces levothyroxine absorption. Added instruction to separate administration by ≥4 hours. TSH check during admission.

Contrast echocardiography needed to evaluate possible LV thrombus identified on standard echo (cannot be excluded in setting of apical akinesis/dyskinesis with LVEF 22%). If contrast echo inconclusive, cardiac MRI needed.
Patient on amiodarone + levothyroxine. Need to confirm adequate thyroid replacement and screen for amiodarone-induced thyroid dysfunction, which can worsen HF.

Anemia (Hgb 11.8) with CKD stage 4. Iron deficiency is common in HF and independently associated with worse outcomes. If ferritin <100 or ferritin 100-300 with TSAT <20%, IV iron is indicated per 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA guidelines (Class IIa).

Cardiac MRI with LGE would definitively evaluate LV thrombus if contrast echo is inconclusive, characterize myocardial fibrosis pattern, and confirm nonischemic etiology. Also valuable for pre-transplant assessment.

stem.presentation: 77-year-old man with a history of systolic and diastolic heart failure, COPD, and ESRD on hemodialysis, admitted for observation after bradycardia, hypotension, and hypoxia during a hemodialysis session. Oxygen saturation was 30% by pleth. His wife reported that during the episode his eyes rolled back and he lost consciousness. CPR was performed for 20-30 seconds with bag-valve mask ventilation before transfer. In the ED he received midodrine 5 mg and a 500 cc bolus without effect and was started on peripheral dopamine for bradycardia. Troponin was 0.45 and was documented as chronically elevated. Cardiology read the ECG as without acute ischemic changes and similar to prior. Bedside echo showed known EF 35% with severe MR, TR. On MICU arrival he was alert and oriented, reported the episode as asymptomatic, and denied fever, chills, chest pain, dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, melena, or hematochezia. He is anuric.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Symptomatic Bradycardia with Syncope/Cardiac Arrest — Atrial Fibrillation with Slow Ventricular Response during Hemodialysis (confidence high).
HF CHARACTERIZATION: phenotype HFrEF (confidence high); etiology ischemic (confidence moderate).
ALSO RANKED PRIMARY: Bradycardia, unspecified.

causes.text: COMPLICATIONS: Syncope and collapse; Hypokalemia.
CONTRIBUTORS: Acute on chronic systolic (left ventricular) heart failure; Mitral valve insufficiency, rheumatic or unspecified; Tricuspid insufficiency, rheumatic or unspecified.

COMORBIDITIES: End-stage renal disease; Dependence on renal dialysis; Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, unspecified; Other and unspecified cirrhosis of liver; Thrombocytopenia, unspecified; Anemia, unspecified; Atherosclerosis of aorta.
HISTORY: Old myocardial infarction.

acute.text: CONTINUE: dopamine IV continuous infusion; vancomycin IV Per HD protocol, trough-guided; cefepime 1000 mg IV q24h (ESRD dosing); nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL PRN chest pain.
acute.detail:
dopamine: Symptomatic bradycardia with hemodynamic compromise Contingency: Wean when HR >60 and SBP >90 sustained. Discontinue after pacemaker implantation.
vancomycin: Empiric coverage for possible sepsis Contingency: Discontinue if cultures negative at 48-72h and clinical improvement. Target trough 15-20.
cefepime: Empiric broad-spectrum coverage for possible sepsis Contingency: Discontinue if cultures negative and clinical improvement. Monitor for neurotoxicity (seizures, encephalopathy) — increased risk in ESRD.
nitroglycerin: Angina relief for CAD Contingency: Use only if SBP >100. Extreme caution given chronic hypotension and concurrent midodrine/dopamine.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: aspirin 81 mg PO daily; clopidogrel 75 mg PO daily; atorvastatin PO daily; midodrine PO TID; pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily; calcium acetate PO TID with meals; paricalcitol PO Per current regimen; tiotropium 18 mcg INH daily; fluticasone-salmeterol 250 mcg INH BID; albuterol 2.5 mg INH PRN; ipratropium-albuterol INH PRN; acyclovir 200 mg PO q12h (ESRD dosing); thiamine 100 mg PO daily; ascorbic acid PO daily.
gdmt.detail:
aspirin: Secondary prevention CAD/prior PCI Contingency: Hold if Plt <50 or active bleeding
clopidogrel: DAPT for prior PCI/CAD Contingency: Discontinue if anticoagulation started or Plt <50 or active bleeding. Consult interventional cardiology for minimum DAPT duration.
atorvastatin: Secondary prevention CAD, high-intensity statin therapy Contingency: Reduce dose if ALT/AST >3x ULN
midodrine: Chronic hypotension Contingency: Wean if SBP consistently >100 after CRT implantation
pantoprazole: GI prophylaxis — DAPT, thrombocytopenia, cirrhosis with portal HTN Contingency: Switched from omeprazole to avoid clopidogrel-omeprazole DDI (reduced antiplatelet efficacy). Pantoprazole has minimal CYP2C19 interaction.
calcium acetate: Hyperphosphatemia management in ESRD Contingency: Adjust per phosphorus and calcium levels
paricalcitol: Secondary hyperparathyroidism in ESRD Contingency: Adjust per PTH, calcium, phosphorus
tiotropium: COPD maintenance
fluticasone-salmeterol: COPD maintenance (ICS/LABA) Contingency: Monitor heart rate — salmeterol (LABA) may have chronotropic effects. Currently beneficial given bradycardia, but reassess after pacemaker.
albuterol: COPD rescue bronchodilator
ipratropium-albuterol: COPD rescue
acyclovir: Antiviral prophylaxis/treatment (likely ocular herpes given ophthalmic meds) Contingency: Ensure renal dose adjustment. Standard doses cause neurotoxicity in ESRD. Monitor for confusion, tremor, myoclonus.
thiamine: Vitamin supplementation — cirrhosis, ESRD
ascorbic acid: Vitamin supplementation Contingency: Limit to ≤250 mg/day — oxalate accumulation risk in ESRD

gdmt.text: HOLD: sacubitril-valsartan PO; carvedilol PO; spironolactone PO; dapagliflozin PO; hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate PO.
gdmt.detail:
sacubitril-valsartan: HFrEF GDMT Pillar 1 — CONTRAINDICATED Contingency: NOT STARTED: ESRD on HD (anuric, no residual renal function), chronic hypotension requiring midodrine, K management challenges on HD. Reassess if hemodynamics improve post-CRT.
carvedilol: HFrEF GDMT Pillar 2 — CONTRAINDICATED currently Contingency: NOT STARTED: Symptomatic bradycardia (AF with slow ventricular response causing syncope/cardiac arrest). Reassess AFTER CRT-P/CRT-D implantation — once pacing ensures adequate rate support, initiate low-dose carvedilol 3.125 mg BID with close monitoring.
spironolactone: HFrEF GDMT Pillar 3 — CONTRAINDICATED Contingency: NOT STARTED: ESRD on HD (anuric), risk of life-threatening hyperkalemia between HD sessions. MRA not recommended in dialysis patients.
dapagliflozin: HFrEF GDMT Pillar 4 — NOT INDICATED Contingency: NOT STARTED: ESRD on HD (anuric, eGFR ~25 on HD). SGLT2 inhibitors require residual renal function for mechanism of action. No evidence of benefit in anuric dialysis patients.
hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate: Alternative vasodilator for HFrEF when ACEi/ARB/ARNi contraindicated Contingency: NOT STARTED currently due to chronic hypotension (on midodrine, baseline SBP ~100/60). REASSESS AFTER CRT implantation — if hemodynamics improve and SBP consistently >100 off midodrine, initiate hydralazine 25 mg TID + isosorbide dinitrate 20 mg TID and titrate cautiously.

monitor.detail: Clopidogrel + omeprazole DDI: omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing clopidogrel activation and antiplatelet efficacy. Replaced with pantoprazole 40 mg daily, which has minimal CYP2C19 interaction. Patient has valid GI indications (DAPT, thrombocytopenia Plt 67, cirrhosis with portal HTN) justifying continued PPI.

Substituted for omeprazole to avoid clopidogrel DDI. Long-term PPI use in elderly (Beers criteria) — justified here by DAPT + thrombocytopenia + cirrhosis with portal HTN. Monitor magnesium levels periodically (ESRD + PPI).

Cefepime neurotoxicity risk is significantly elevated in ESRD (eGFR 24.6). Dose of 1g q24h is appropriate for ESRD, but monitor closely for encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures. Consider cefepime level if available.

Acyclovir 200 mg q12h is appropriate ESRD dosing for prophylaxis. However, acyclovir neurotoxicity (confusion, tremor, hallucinations) is increased in ESRD. Monitor neurological status. Ensure adequate removal during HD sessions.

Only bedside echo available — need formal comprehensive TTE with: LV wall thickness (amyloid evaluation), diastolic assessment (E/e'), RV function (TAPSE, S'), RVSP estimation, strain imaging with apical sparing pattern assessment, and formal quantification of severe MR/TR. Critical for amyloidosis workup and CRT planning.
NT-proBNP not measured. Essential for HF severity assessment and prognostication. Disproportionately elevated NT-proBNP relative to EF is a red flag for cardiac amyloidosis.
Serial ECGs to monitor QTc trend, assess for pauses, and document rate/rhythm stability on dopamine. Baseline for comparison post-pacemaker.
Iron studies needed to evaluate iron deficiency anemia in ESRD patient (Hgb 9.3). IV iron may reduce HF hospitalizations in HD patients per PIVOTAL trial.
Thyroid function assessment — hypothyroidism can cause bradycardia and worsen HF. Must exclude as reversible contributor to slow ventricular response.
